articles.title: This legendary board game could take decades to complete
articles.dek: Andy Taeger & James Purcell are trying to become the first people ever complete the board game Campaign for North Africa. The is so complex it could take decades to finish.

paragraphs.en: Andy Taeger & James Purcell are trying to become the first people ever complete the board game Campaign for North Africa. The is so complex it could take decades to finish.
paragraphs.zh: 安迪·泰格和詹姆斯·珀塞尔正试图成为有史以来第一个完成桌面游戏《北非战役》的玩家。这个游戏如此复杂，可能需要几十年才能完成。

paragraphs.en: In the U.K., two friends have begun a challenge that many people believe is impossible. The board game Campaign for North Africa is legendary for its complexity and detail and its extreme time commitment. Andy Taeger and James Purcell are trying to become the first people ever to complete it. Hi to both of you.
paragraphs.zh: 在英国，两个朋友开始了一项许多人认为不可能完成的挑战。棋盘游戏《北非战役》以其复杂性、细节丰富和极高的时间投入而闻名。安迪·泰格和詹姆斯·珀塞尔正试图成为有史以来第一个完成它的人。向你们两位问好。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: So this board game covers a period of World War II that lasted roughly three years. Yet the game itself could take almost 10 times that, you know, many years more. What is it that makes it what you guys have described as comically complicated?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：所以这个棋盘游戏涵盖了二战时期大约三年的时间。然而，游戏本身可能需要几乎十倍的时间，你知道，也就是多年。究竟是什么让它变成了你们所描述的滑稽复杂？

paragraphs.en: PURCELL: I suppose, first and foremost, we aren't generals. So we have no experience in warfare. There is everything to keep track of in this game down to how much water each unit has to drink, how much of that water evaporates, just about every granular detail you can think of.
paragraphs.zh: 普塞尔：我想，最重要的是，我们不是将军。因此我们没有战争经验。在这个游戏中，有太多事情需要跟踪，包括每个单位需要喝多少水、有多少水会蒸发，你能想到的几乎每一个细节。

paragraphs.en: TAEGER: There's a rule Italian infantry uses more water so they could boil their pasta.
paragraphs.zh: TAEGER：意大利步兵有一个规定，就是使用更多的水，这样他们就可以煮意大利面。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: The pasta is that the Italians are going to go through drinking water faster, and they need to calculate that in?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：意大利人喝水会更快，而他们需要把这一点计算在内吗？

paragraphs.en: PURCELL: Yeah. Apparently, they have to use more to boil their pasta. I'm not sure how accurate that is, but that's part of the rules.
paragraphs.zh: 普塞尔：是的。显然，他们必须用更多的水来煮意大利面。我不确定这有多准确，但这是规则的一部分。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: All right, so the big question is - why? Why are the two of you doing this, if you know it could take years or even decades to complete?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：好吧，那么大问题是——为什么？如果你们知道这可能需要几年甚至几十年才能完成，你们为什么还要做这件事？

paragraphs.en: PURCELL: We'd love to give an answer that makes some aspect of sense, but we really don't know why we're doing this.
paragraphs.zh: 珀塞尔：我们很希望给出一个有某种意义的回答，但我们真的不知道自己为什么要这样做。

articles.title: 'Grasping at straws': Judge dismisses Trump suit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
articles.dek: Saying the president was "grasping at straws," a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story…

paragraphs.en: Saying the president was "grasping at straws," a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.
paragraphs.zh: 一位联邦法官在周六表示，总统是在“抓救命稻草”，并驳回了唐纳德·特朗普针对《华尔街日报》和媒体大亨鲁珀特·默多克关于报道他与杰弗里·爱泼斯坦关系的新闻提起的100亿美元诉讼。

paragraphs.en: U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the suit with prejudice, ruling that the president did not prove the defendants made defamatory statements with actual malice as required by law. The ruling said the lawsuit had attempted to "manufacture" flaws in the Journal's investigative reporting.
paragraphs.zh: 迈阿密的美国地方法官达林·盖尔斯（Darrin Gayles）以有偏见的方式驳回了这起诉讼，裁定总统未能证明被告按照法律要求以实际恶意发表了诽谤性言论。裁决指出，这起诉讼试图“捏造”《华尔街日报》调查报道中的缺陷。

paragraphs.en: When a case is thrown out "with prejudice," it cannot be refiled again and the dismissal is permanent and incontrovertible.
paragraphs.zh: 当案件被以“有偏见”的理由驳回时，不能再次提起诉讼，该驳回是永久且无可争辩的。

paragraphs.en: The dismissal is a blow to Trump and his administration, which have both pursued adversarial relationships with news organizations during his second term. In addition to the Journal, he is embroiled in lawsuits involving the BBC, The Associated Press and — most recently — CNN, MS NOW and Politico, which are suing him for restored access after he banished them from the White House in mid-September.
paragraphs.zh: 这次解职对特朗普及其政府是一次打击，他们在第二任期内一直与新闻机构保持对抗关系。除了《华尔街日报》，他还卷入了涉及英国广播公司、美联社以及——最近——CNN、MS NOW和Politico的诉讼，这些机构正在起诉他以恢复访问权限，此前他在九月中旬将它们驱逐出白宫。

paragraphs.en: Trump has denounced media outlets that write things to which he objects and frequently calls them "fake news" and insults their journalists.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普谴责那些写出他反对内容的媒体，并经常称它们为“假新闻”，还侮辱它们的记者。

paragraphs.en: The White House did not immediately react publicly to Saturday's dismissal or respond to an AP request for comment.
paragraphs.zh: 白宫没有立即就周六的解雇作出公开反应，也没有回应美联社的置评请求。

paragraphs.en: The lawsuit against the Journal was over a story it published last year describing a sexually suggestive letter and drawing that the paper said bore Trump's name and was included in a 2003 album compiled for Epstein's 50th birthday.
paragraphs.zh: 对该报的诉讼是关于它去年发表的一篇报道，该报道描述了一封具有性暗示的信件和一幅画，报纸称这些信件和画作署有特朗普的名字，并被收录在为爱泼斯坦50岁生日编制的2003年相册中。

paragraphs.en: The letter was reportedly collected by disgraced British socialite Ghislaine Maxwell as part of a birthday album for Epstein years before he was first arrested in 2006 and subsequently had a falling-out with Trump.
paragraphs.zh: 据报道，这封信是由声名狼藉的英国社交名流吉丝兰·麦克斯韦收集的，作为为埃普斯坦制作的生日相册的一部分，这发生在他2006年首次被逮捕之前的几年，之后他与特朗普反目成仇。

articles.title: Your writing was flagged as AI. What does that actually mean?
articles.dek: Ghostwriter Sally McGraw was hoping to land a job developing a book proposal for a prospective client. But after submitting a writing sample, she got an unexpected response: an email telling her…

paragraphs.en: Ghostwriter Sally McGraw was hoping to land a job developing a book proposal for a prospective client. But after submitting a writing sample, she got an unexpected response: an email telling her that multiple artificial intelligence detection tools had flagged her work as machine-generated.
paragraphs.zh: 代笔作家萨莉·麦格劳希望获得一份为潜在客户开发书籍提案的工作。但在提交写作样本后，她收到了一份意想不到的回复：一封电子邮件告诉她，多个人工智能检测工具已经将她的作品标记为机器生成。

paragraphs.en: "I was floored because I had not used AI to generate the text," McGraw said. "I'd written it all myself."
paragraphs.zh: 麦格劳说：“我震惊了，因为我没有用人工智能来生成这段文字，我完全是自己写的。”

paragraphs.en: Having spent more than 20 years as a professional nonfiction writer, McGraw said she was angry that her work had been dismissed as AI-written.
paragraphs.zh: 麦格劳说，作为一名拥有超过20年经验的专业非虚构作家，她对自己的作品被认为是人工智能写的而感到愤怒。

paragraphs.en: "You know where you see a cartoon character going red from their chin all the way up to the crown of their head? I felt my ears starting to burn," she said. "I thought, what is going on?"
paragraphs.zh: “你知道在卡通里你看到一个角色从下巴一直红到头顶的情景吗？我感觉我的耳朵也开始发热了，”她说。“我当时想，发生什么事了？”

paragraphs.en: McGraw said she assured the client she had written the proposal herself, but decided not to press the issue because she considered the job "minor."
paragraphs.zh: 麦格劳说她向客户保证自己亲自撰写了提案，但她决定不再坚持这个问题，因为她认为这份工作“微不足道”。

paragraphs.en: In an email to NPR, the client confirmed that she had screened McGraw's work for AI. But she said the results were not the determining factor in choosing to hire a different writer, instead citing experience and fit. McGraw says she was paid for her writing samples, but believes the detector results cost her the opportunity to write the full book proposal.
paragraphs.zh: 在给NPR的电子邮件中，这位客户确认她已经对麦格劳的作品进行了人工智能检测。但她表示，检测结果并不是选择雇用其他作者的决定性因素，而是引用了经验和契合度。麦格劳表示，她为自己的写作样本获得了报酬，但认为检测结果让她失去了撰写完整书籍提案的机会。

paragraphs.en: As editors struggle to keep up with a growing influx of AI-generated content, some are turning to detection tools to help sift through the mounting number of submissions. But these tools aren't perfect: They've been known to falsely flag human-written work as AI, which can leave writers with little idea of what triggered the result and how to prove otherwise.
paragraphs.zh: 随着编辑们努力跟上不断增长的 AI 生成内容，一些人开始使用检测工具来帮助筛选不断增加的投稿数量。但这些工具并不完美：它们已知会错误地将人工撰写的作品标记为 AI，这可能让作者对触发结果的原因几乎一无所知，也不知如何证明其作品是人工创作的。

paragraphs.en: "Everyone knows that these screeners are not 100% accurate," said McGraw.
paragraphs.zh: 麦格劳说：“每个人都知道这些筛查器并不是百分之百准确。”

articles.title: Oyster stocks have plunged in the Chesapeake. This resident wants to bring them back
articles.dek: John Consoli stands on the edge of his pier, which juts out from the southern tip of Maryland's Kent Island and into the Chesapeake Bay. He leans over and hoists a mesh the size and shape of a…

paragraphs.en: John Consoli stands on the edge of his pier, which juts out from the southern tip of Maryland's Kent Island and into the Chesapeake Bay. He leans over and hoists a mesh the size and shape of a pillowcase out of the water.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰·康索利站在他码头的尽头，码头从马里兰州肯特岛的南端伸入切萨皮克湾。他俯身，将一个大小和形状像枕头套的网从水中提起。

paragraphs.en: It's packed with oysters. He manages to get it onto the pier. "These are brand new oysters from this year," he says. "When I got them, they weighed nothing. And this is just three months of growth. The net is chock full, I can hardly pull it up."
paragraphs.zh: 里面满是牡蛎。他设法把它弄到码头上。“这些是今年的新牡蛎，”他说。“当我拿到它们时，几乎没重量。这只是三个月的生长。网满得不得了，我几乎拉不上来。”

paragraphs.en: Once he catches his breath, Consoli marvels at these molluscs. "I think I'm more enthusiastic about something that's like a rock than anybody else could possibly be," he says with a big grin. "I really can't think of many more creatures that do the good that oysters do."
paragraphs.zh: 一旦他喘过气来，康索利对这些软体动物感到惊讶。他咧着大大的笑容说：“我想我对像石头一样的东西的热情，比其他任何人可能都要高。”他接着说：“我真的想不出还有多少生物能像牡蛎那样带来好处。”

paragraphs.en: Oysters underpin the Chesapeake's coastal and estuarine ecosystem. Each adult filters up to 50 gallons of water a day. Cleaner water leads to a healthier bay and more sea grass. "That helps crabs and other organisms," says Consoli.
paragraphs.zh: 牡蛎支撑着切萨皮克湾的沿海和河口生态系统。每只成牡蛎每天可以过滤多达50加仑的水。水质更清洁意味着海湾更健康，海草更多。“这对螃蟹和其他生物都有帮助，”康索利说。

paragraphs.en: Plus, oyster shells are a habitat unto themselves. "Because of all the nooks and crannies," he explains, "a lot of small fish and crabs live and eat amongst them and hide, so it creates a biodiverse environment. I even found a seahorse, which was incredible. I've never seen a seahorse in my life!"
paragraphs.zh: 此外，牡蛎壳本身就是一个栖息地。他解释说：“因为有各种各样的缝隙和角落，很多小鱼和螃蟹在其中生活、觅食和藏身，所以它创造了一个生物多样化的环境。我甚至发现了一只海马，这太不可思议了。我这辈子从未见过海马！”

paragraphs.en: Oyster reefs used to abound in the Chesapeake, but overharvesting decimated their ranks — by over 99% by 2011, according to one estimate. This monumental shift in the bay contributed to poorer water quality and less habitat for other species.
paragraphs.zh: 牡蛎礁曾经在切萨皮克湾大量存在，但过度捕捞摧毁了它们的数量——据一项估计，到2011年减少了超过99%。这一巨大变化导致海湾水质下降，并为其他物种留下的栖息地减少。

paragraphs.en: Oyster farming in the Chesapeake has expanded in recent years, despite environmental and disease challenges, says Ryan Carnegie, a biologist at the Virginia Institute of Marine Science. He adds that wild oysters have also made a partial comeback, helped by better management and investments in restoration. But, says Elizabeth North, a fisheries oceanographer at the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science, "current oyster populations are likely still a fraction of these historic populations."
paragraphs.zh: 弗吉尼亚海洋科学研究所的生物学家瑞安·卡内基表示，尽管面临环境和疾病的挑战，近年来切萨皮克湾的牡蛎养殖业仍在扩大。他补充说，野生牡蛎也部分恢复，这得益于更好的管理和对修复工作的投资。但是，马里兰大学环境科学中心的渔业海洋学家伊丽莎白·诺斯表示，“当前的牡蛎种群可能仍只是历史种群的一小部分。”

paragraphs.en: Consoli's goal, therefore, is to be a caretaker of sorts, stocking the bay with ever more oysters and looking after their wellbeing. He floats them just below the surface where he says the nutrients are concentrated to help them grow quickly. And although his oysters aren't intended for eating, a cleaner bay does mean better habitat for those that are harvested commercially.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，Consoli 的目标是成为某种照管者，为海湾储存越来越多的牡蛎并照顾它们的健康。他将牡蛎漂浮在水面下方，他说那里营养物质集中，有助于它们快速生长。尽管他的牡蛎并不用于食用，但清洁的海湾确实意味着为商业采收的牡蛎提供了更好的栖息环境。

articles.title: At a Moscow movie screening, Anthony Bourdain's Russian fixer remembers the late chef
articles.dek: Zamir Gotta, Anthony Bourdain's longtime fixer in Russia, remembers working with and becoming friends with the late chef.

paragraphs.en: Zamir Gotta, Anthony Bourdain's longtime fixer in Russia, remembers working with and becoming friends with the late chef.
paragraphs.zh: 扎米尔·戈塔，安东尼·布尔丹在俄罗斯的长期联络人，回忆起与已故厨师共事并成为朋友的时光。

paragraphs.en: Eight years after the death of Anthony Bourdain, people around the world still mourn the chef, author and TV star. At a movie theater in Moscow, hundreds of Russian fans gathered in September for the premiere of "Tony," the new Hollywood film based on Bourdain's early life. Among them was a man Bourdain loved to call International Man of Mystery. He's someone who became central to Bourdain's success in Russia and beyond. NPR's Charles Maynes reports from Moscow. And a note - this story includes mention of suicide.
paragraphs.zh: 在安东尼·布尔丹去世八年后，全世界的人们仍在悼念这位厨师、作家和电视明星。在莫斯科的一家电影院，数百名俄罗斯影迷于九月聚集，观看基于布尔丹早年生活的新好莱坞电影《托尼》的首映式。其中有一位布尔丹喜欢称之为“国际神秘人”的男子。他是一个在俄罗斯及其他地方对布尔丹的成功起到关键作用的人。NPR的查尔斯·梅因斯从莫斯科报道。此外，提示——本故事提及自杀内容。

paragraphs.en: CHARLES MAYNES, BYLINE: Oysters on the half shell, bottles of imported beer, Peroni, if you must know. Russia may be under Western sanctions, but at last month's Moscow premiere of the film "Tony," the Russian Organizers pulled out all the stops to honor Anthony Bourdain, the American chef, travel writer and something of a life coach to so many, even here.
paragraphs.zh: 查尔斯·梅恩斯，署名：半壳生蚝，进口啤酒，如果你一定要知道的话，是佩罗尼。在俄罗斯可能受到西方制裁之际，但在上个月莫斯科举行的电影《托尼》首映礼上，俄罗斯主办方竭尽全力向美国厨师、旅游作家，以及对许多人来说甚至是生活导师的安东尼·布尔丹致敬。

paragraphs.en: KATERINA KODENKA: My shirt says, God, I miss Anthony Bourdain.
paragraphs.zh: 卡特里娜·科登卡：我的衬衫上写着，天啊，我想念安东尼·布尔丹。

paragraphs.en: MAYNES: Katerina Kodenka (ph), a recent university graduate who attended the screening, says Bourdain has been one of her heroes since she was a teenager. In an age seemingly dominated by war and hate, Kodenka says Bourdain's TV essays and writings point the way towards a better world.

articles.title: Secretary Rubio has a tough time getting officials at G20 on the same page
articles.dek: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is hosting the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, with a focus on economic and security challenges.

paragraphs.en: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is hosting the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, with a focus on economic and security challenges.
paragraphs.zh: 美国国务卿马尔科·鲁比奥正在亚特兰大主持二十国集团外长会议，重点关注经济和安全挑战。

paragraphs.en: Tensions flared this weekend at a meeting chaired by Secretary of State Marco Rubio of the Group of 20 leading economies. NPR's Michele Kelemen reports from Atlanta.
paragraphs.zh: 本周末，在由二十国集团主要经济体的国务卿马尔科·鲁比奥主持的会议上，紧张局势升级。NPR的米歇尔·凯莱门从亚特兰大报道。

paragraphs.en: MICHELE KELEMEN, BYLINE: There was no joint communiqué or even a family photo. Several foreign ministers did not want to be in a picture with Russia's Sergey Lavrov. So Rubio canceled plans for that, but he says countries did come together around some big themes, including freedom of navigation.
paragraphs.zh: MICHELE KELEMEN，署名记者：没有联合公报，甚至没有家庭合影。几位外长不愿意与俄罗斯的谢尔盖·拉夫罗夫合影。因此，鲁比奥取消了这一计划，但他说各国确实在一些重大主题上达成了共识，包括航行自由。

paragraphs.en: MARCO RUBIO: Safe passage of vessels in international waters is vital to the livelihood of the world. And we now live in a world where the Iranian regime actively and openly targets commercial vessels.
paragraphs.zh: 马克·鲁比奥：船只在国际水域的安全通行对世界的生计至关重要。而我们现在生活在一个伊朗政权公开并积极针对商业船只的世界中。

paragraphs.en: KELEMEN: He says the U.S. is open to diplomacy with Iran, but he wouldn't rule out a new round of attacks, even as the U.S. military tries to keep the Strait of Hormuz open.
paragraphs.zh: 凯莱门：他说美国对与伊朗的外交持开放态度，但他不会排除新的攻击，尽管美国军方试图保持霍尔木兹海峡通行。

paragraphs.en: RUBIO: Central Command in the United States has done a phenomenal job of protecting this shipping. And today, the amount of fuel getting through there is comparable with what was coming out before the conflict. But nonetheless, we've had to defend these ships from drones and missiles almost every single night.
paragraphs.zh: 鲁比奥：美国中央司令部在保护这些航运方面做得非常出色。如今，通过那里的燃料数量与冲突前的水平相当。但尽管如此，我们几乎每个晚上都必须保护这些船只免受无人机和导弹的袭击。

paragraphs.en: KELEMEN: Other G20 countries are worried about the potential for a new escalation in the Middle East. Europeans are also nervous about U.S. sanctions relief to Russia. Germany's foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, is trying to highlight the positive, saying, while they may not agree on tactics, everyone shares the goal of getting Russia to the negotiating table to end the war in Ukraine.
paragraphs.zh: KELEMEN：其他G20国家担心中东地区可能出现新的升级。欧洲人对于美国对俄罗斯的制裁缓解也感到紧张。德国外交部长约翰·瓦德富尔试图强调积极的一面，他说，虽然他们在具体策略上可能意见不一，但大家的共同目标是让俄罗斯坐上谈判桌，以结束乌克兰战争。

paragraphs.en: JOHANN WADEPHUL: In the substance, we have the same position, not only in Europe, but together also with the United States of America. And for us, Marco Rubio was always a reliable partner.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰·瓦德富尔：在实质上，我们的立场是相同的，不仅在欧洲，而且与美利坚合众国一起。对我们来说，马可·鲁比奥一直是一个可靠的合作伙伴。

articles.title: Mixed economic forecast weighs heavy ahead of midterms
articles.dek: There was a mixed Halloween bag of economic news this week. GDP growth is up, but so are prices. For now at least, interest rates are staying the same. What does that mean for the midterm elections?

paragraphs.en: There was a mixed Halloween bag of economic news this week. GDP growth is up, but so are prices. For now at least, interest rates are staying the same. What does that mean for the midterm elections?
paragraphs.zh: 本周的经济消息五花八门，像是混合的万圣节礼包。国内生产总值增长了，但物价也在上涨。至少目前，利率保持不变。这对中期选举意味着什么？

paragraphs.en: As we just heard, many midterm races are extremely tight. And for voters, the economy has consistently ranked as a top issue driving them to the polls. This week, just days away from Election Day, we got some key economic news. New GDP numbers show the U.S. economy is growing at a healthy clip, but inflation remains stubbornly high. The Federal Reserve met and decided not to raise interest rates, but higher borrowing costs could still be in store by the end of the year. So what does that mean for the midterms? NPR's Scott Horsley is with us to explain.
paragraphs.zh: 正如我们刚刚听到的，许多中期选举的竞赛十分激烈。对于选民来说，经济一直被认为是促使他们去投票的首要问题。本周，距离选举日仅有几天之际，我们得到了一些关键的经济消息。新的国内生产总值数据表明，美国经济正在以健康的速度增长，但通货膨胀仍然顽固地高企。美联储召开会议并决定不提高利率，但到今年年底，借贷成本可能仍会上升。那么，这对中期选举意味着什么呢？NPR的斯科特·霍斯利（Scott Horsley）将为我们解释。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: So affordability, that word we hear over and over and over again. It's at the top of mind of so many voters. What is the new economic data tell us about that?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：所以可负担性，这个词我们一次又一次地听到。它在许多选民心中占据首位。新的经济数据告诉我们关于这一点什么？

paragraphs.en: HORSLEY: Well, it tells us affordability is still a challenge. You know, the cost of living keeps going up, and people's paychecks are not keeping pace. This week, the Commerce Department clocked inflation in September at 3.6%. That's higher than the month before. And significantly, it's higher than it was when President Trump returned to the White House. That's a big reason nearly two-thirds of Americans disapprove of the president's economic stewardship. Voters punished Democrats for inflation back in 2024, and they may decide to punish Republicans this time around.
paragraphs.zh: 霍斯利：嗯，这告诉我们，负担能力仍然是一个挑战。你知道，生活成本不断上升，而人们的工资却跟不上步伐。本周，商务部公布九月份的通胀率为3.6%。这比上个月高。而且，值得注意的是，这比特朗普总统回到白宫时还要高。这是近三分之二美国人不赞成总统经济管理的一个重要原因。选民在2024年因通胀而惩罚了民主党，而这次他们可能会决定惩罚共和党。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: Yet we have the seeming contradiction, which is that the latest numbers show the economy is growing. So why isn't that registering or paying off for ordinary voters?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：然而我们有一个看似矛盾的情况，那就是最新数据表明经济在增长。那么，为什么这对普通选民来说没有反映出来或带来收益呢？

paragraphs.en: HORSLEY: Yeah. The economy did perk up a bit in late summer and early fall. GDP, which is the broadest measure of economic activity, grew at an annual rate of 3.4% in July, August and September. That's up from 2.2% the previous quarter. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said this past week, that's a good sign.
paragraphs.zh: 霍斯利：是的。经济在晚夏和初秋确实有所回升。国内生产总值（GDP），这是衡量经济活动最广泛的指标，在七月、八月和九月的年增长率为3.4%。相比上一季度的2.2%有所上升。美联储主席凯文·沃什上周表示，这是一个好迹象。

paragraphs.en: KEVIN WARSH: The economy is strong. The economy is pointing in the right direction.
paragraphs.zh: 凯文·沃什：经济很强劲。经济正朝着正确的方向发展。

paragraphs.en: HORSLEY: But a lot of that GDP growth is being driven by the huge investment in artificial intelligence. And, you know, if you build data centers for a living, you're pretty busy these days. But otherwise, this burst of economic growth has not been accompanied by a burst of new jobs.
paragraphs.zh: HORSLEY：但是，GDP 的大部分增长是由对人工智能的大量投资推动的。而且，你知道，如果你的工作是建造数据中心，那么最近你会非常忙。不过，除此之外，这波经济增长并没有伴随大量新工作的增加。

paragraphs.en: PFEIFFER: And, Scott, what about the job market? What about unemployment numbers?
paragraphs.zh: PFEIFFER：那么，斯科特，就业市场情况如何？失业数字呢？

articles.title: Wild West crypto: Staggering Binance heist exposes sector fragility
articles.dek: A massive cyber heist of crypto exchange Binance is exposing some of the fragilities of the sector and reinforcing perceptions of the industry as a financial Wild West, critics warn.

paragraphs.en: A massive cyber heist of crypto exchange Binance is exposing some of the fragilities of the sector and reinforcing perceptions of the industry as a financial Wild West, critics warn.
paragraphs.zh: 批评人士警告称，对加密交易所币安的大规模网络盗窃正在暴露该行业的一些脆弱性，并强化了人们对该行业像金融西部荒野一样的看法。

paragraphs.en: This week, hackers stole more than $6 billion from the Binance Crypto Exchange, the biggest heist in the history of cryptocurrency. The incident is sparking new fears about that sector, sometimes called Wild West of finance, and it comes as the crypto industry has been trying to gain broader respectability under a friendly administration. We're joined now by NPR senior business editor Rafael Nam. Rafael, thanks so much for being with us.
paragraphs.zh: 本周，黑客从币安加密货币交易所窃取了超过60亿美元，这是加密货币历史上最大的抢劫案件。该事件引发了人们对这一行业的新担忧，这个行业有时被称为金融的“狂野西部”，而此时加密货币行业正试图在一个友好的政府下获得更广泛的认可。我们现在请来了NPR资深商业编辑拉斐尔·南。拉斐尔，非常感谢你与我们同在。

paragraphs.en: SIMON: How did this happen? How did they lose so much money?
paragraphs.zh: 西蒙：这是怎么发生的？他们怎么会亏这么多钱？

paragraphs.en: NAM: I know. It's a staggering amount. So a group of hackers, widely believed to be the North Korean military, broke into accounts that investors hold at Binance to trade cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin and then stole their money, essentially. Now Binance has promised to repay anybody who lost money and is working hard at recovering as much of it as it can. The company says they've managed to freeze about $3 billion of the stolen crypto.
paragraphs.zh: NAM: 我知道。这是一个令人震惊的数额。所以，有一群黑客，人们普遍认为是朝鲜军方，入侵了投资者在币安持有的账户，以交易比特币等加密货币，然后本质上窃取了他们的资金。现在币安承诺会偿还任何损失的钱，并且正在努力追回尽可能多的资金。公司表示他们已经成功冻结了约30亿美元的被盗加密货币。

paragraphs.en: SIMON: You don't often hear about so much money being taken - stolen from a financial exchange. How did it happen?
paragraphs.zh: 西蒙：你不常听到从金融交易所窃取这么多钱的事情。这是怎么发生的？

paragraphs.en: NAM: Yeah. I mean, so there's still a lot we don't know, Scott. And it's too early to say whether there were any major flaws at Binance's security systems. If anything, researchers I talk to say it may have more to do with how sophisticated North Korean hackers are. But the one thing critics did point out is that the way these crypto exchanges are set up deserves some scrutiny here.
paragraphs.zh: NAM：是的。我是说，Scott，我们仍然有很多不清楚的地方。现在说币安的安全系统是否存在重大缺陷还为时过早。无论如何，我接触的一些研究人员表示，这可能更多地与朝鲜黑客的高水平技术有关。但批评者指出的一点是，这些加密货币交易所的设立方式确实值得关注。

paragraphs.en: What's peculiar is that at crypto exchanges, you can not only buy and sell Bitcoin, for example, you can also hold that Bitcoin at a trading account at the exchange itself. That's a very unique and risky feature that makes it different from traditional stock exchanges, according to Amanda Fischer from financial advocacy group Better Markets.
paragraphs.zh: 奇怪的是，在加密货币交易所，你不仅可以买卖比特币，例如，你还可以在交易所的交易账户中持有比特币。金融宣传组织Better Markets的阿曼达·费舍尔表示，这是一个非常独特且高风险的特性，使其不同于传统的股票交易所。

paragraphs.en: AMANDA FISCHER: You may trade on the New York Stock Exchange, but you don't keep your funds with the New York Stock Exchange. You keep it with your broker. And your broker is audited and regulated by the SEC, and your broker has to pay for insurance that will make customers whole in the event that there's a cyberattack.
paragraphs.zh: 阿曼达·费舍尔：你可以在纽约证券交易所交易，但你不会将资金存放在纽约证券交易所。你是将资金存放在你的经纪人那里。你的经纪人接受美国证券交易委员会的审计和监管，并且你的经纪人必须购买保险，以在发生网络攻击时保障客户的资金安全。

articles.title: Plans for a data center threaten scenic wilderness and dark skies in West Virginia
articles.dek: DAVIS, W.Va. — Stretching nearly a million acres through the rugged mountains of eastern West Virginia, the Monongahela National Forest links some of the state's best known natural attractions.…

paragraphs.en: DAVIS, W.Va. — Stretching nearly a million acres through the rugged mountains of eastern West Virginia, the Monongahela National Forest links some of the state's best known natural attractions. The vast area ranges from the ski slopes of Canaan Valley to the dark skies of Blackwater Falls and Spruce Knob and includes the small towns of Davis and Thomas that serve as gateways for visitors to the region.
paragraphs.zh: 西弗吉尼亚州戴维斯——蒙农加希拉国家森林横跨西弗吉尼亚东部崎岖的山脉，面积近一百万英亩，连接了该州一些最著名的自然景点。这片广阔的区域从卡南谷的滑雪坡延伸到布莱克沃特瀑布和云杉峰的黑暗天空，并包括戴维斯和托马斯这两个小镇，作为游客前往该地区的门户。

paragraphs.en: For the past seven months, Kaleb Skelton, his wife, Ella, their 2-year-old son, Ryder, and dog Mabel have lived in a camper in this corner of West Virginia's "almost heaven." Kaleb is finishing a seasonal stint as a campground manager on a lake near Spruce Knob, the state's highest point.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去的七个月里，Kaleb Skelton、他的妻子Ella、他们两岁的儿子Ryder以及他们的狗Mabel一直住在西弗吉尼亚州这个“几乎是天堂”的角落里的一个露营车里。Kaleb正在完成他作为Spruce Knob附近一个湖泊露营地经理的季节性工作，Spruce Knob是该州的最高点。

paragraphs.en: On clear nights atop the isolated peak, they get to experience a river of stars in one of the very few pockets of darkness remaining in the Eastern United States. The area has become a draw for amateur astronomers.
paragraphs.zh: 在那座孤立山峰的晴朗夜晚，他们可以在美国东部残留的少数黑暗区域之一中，亲身体验到星河。该区域已成为业余天文学家的热门之地。

paragraphs.en: During summer's new moons, Kaleb says, one in four campsites he oversees is occupied by someone with a telescope. He thought his family's cabin in eastern Texas offered "the craziest" dark skies he'd ever seen, "but coming out here definitely rivals it."
paragraphs.zh: 在夏天的新月期间，卡勒布说，他监管的四个营地中就有一个会有带望远镜的人。他曾认为自己家位于德克萨斯州东部的小木屋拥有“他见过的最疯狂的”黑暗天空，“但来到这里绝对可以与之媲美。”

paragraphs.en: Those inky-black nights — and the natural beauty they shelter — are now under threat from what many residents see as a modern-day version of extractive industries like logging and mining that once defined the region. In a place where tourism, outdoor recreation and community are deeply intertwined, a gigantic power plant and data center campus in nearby Tucker County would bring large-scale development into the heart of it all.
paragraphs.zh: 那些漆黑的夜晚——以及它们所孕育的自然美景——现在正受到威胁，许多居民认为这种威胁是现代版的开采业，就像曾经定义该地区的伐木和采矿业一样。在一个旅游业、户外活动和社区紧密交织的地方，附近塔克县的一座巨型发电厂和数据中心园区将把大规模开发带入这一切的中心。

paragraphs.en: A stark image of the town of Davis from 1885, during the heyday of logging, is a reminder of that transformation. The photo shows a handful of squat buildings amid a broad clearing littered with forest remains.
paragraphs.zh: 1885年戴维斯镇的一个鲜明画面，在伐木业鼎盛时期，提醒人们那一转变。这张照片显示，在一片布满森林残骸的宽阔空地上，零星分布着几栋矮小的建筑。

paragraphs.en: They used to call it "Stump Town," says Kim Williams, president of the Snow Sports Museum of West Virginia in Canaan Valley. At the turn of the century, massive first-growth trees dominated the landscape.

articles.title: Drone photo award winners: Far-out landscapes. Ship recycling. Rugs, rugs rugs!
articles.dek: It looks like a spacecraft that settled gently onto a golden beach.

paragraphs.en: It looks like a spacecraft that settled gently onto a golden beach.
paragraphs.zh: 它看起来像一艘轻轻降落在金色沙滩上的宇宙飞船。

paragraphs.en: Off the coast of Bangladesh, an enormous vessel lies stranded on the mudflats, its steel hull partially dismantled as workers mill around it. This unusual aerial view of a tanker, specially designed to transport liquified natural gas used for cooking, electricity and transport, won photographer George Steinmetz the top prize — overall winner of the 2026 Siena Drone Photo Awards.
paragraphs.zh: 在孟加拉国海岸，一艘巨大的船只搁浅在泥滩上，其钢制船体部分被拆解，工人们在周围忙碌。这张罕见的航空视角照片拍摄的是一艘专门设计用于运输液化天然气（用于烹饪、电力和交通）的油轮，这张照片让摄影师乔治·斯坦梅茨赢得了2026年锡耶纳无人机摄影奖的最高奖——总冠军。

paragraphs.en: Each year, the Siena Drone Photo Awards highlight bird's-eye views of our planet, revealing landscapes, livelihoods and human stories often invisible from the ground. Here, we've selected some of this year's winning and highly commended photographs, focusing on the countries of the Global South.
paragraphs.zh: 每年，锡耶纳无人机摄影奖都会展示我们星球的鸟瞰图，揭示从地面往往看不见的景观、生活方式和人类故事。在这里，我们挑选了今年的一些获奖和特别表彰的照片，重点关注全球南方的国家。

paragraphs.en: In an interview with NPR, Steinmetz says he's been long fascinated by Bangladesh's shipbreaking industry, where enormous vessels from around the globe, nearing the end of their working lives, are dismantled and their materials recovered for reuse. The photograph is titled "Shipbreaking on the mudflats, Bay of Bengal." Steinmetz sent up his drone north of Chattogram (Chittagong), along this 13-mile coastal strip, offering a stark glimpse into what this industry is like.
paragraphs.zh: 在接受NPR采访时，斯坦梅茨表示，他长期以来一直对孟加拉国的拆船业着迷，这里来自世界各地的巨型船只在接近使用寿命结束时被拆解，其材料被回收再利用。这张照片的标题是《孟加拉湾泥滩上的拆船》。斯坦梅茨将他的无人机送到吉大港（Chattogram/Chittagong）以北，沿着这条13英里的海岸线拍摄，展示了这个行业的真实面貌。

paragraphs.en: He was exploring the relationship between human populations and the environment for a book project and saw the industry as an extraordinary example of recycling on a vast scale.
paragraphs.zh: 他正在为一本书的项目探索人类群体与环境之间的关系，并将这个行业视为大规模回收的一个非凡例子。

paragraphs.en: Photographing it proved surprisingly difficult. The ship breaking industry has faced criticism from environmental organizations, human rights groups, labor unions and non-governmental organizations for its unchecked pollution, the leeching of chemicals into the sea and dangerous working conditions. Shipyard owners are wary of journalists and photographers. Local photographers initially warned Steinmetz that securing access might be nearly impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 拍摄它出乎意料地困难。拆船行业因其无法控制的污染、化学物质渗入海洋以及危险的工作条件，已受到环保组织、人权团体、工会和非政府组织的批评。船厂老板对记者和摄影师持谨慎态度。当地的摄影师最初警告施坦梅茨，获得进入许可可能几乎不可能。

paragraphs.en: Undeterred, he surveyed and photographed the entire coastline north of Chattogram with his drone, searching for a vessel that would make an especially striking photograph. He eventually settled on the liquid natural gas tanker. "The trick for me was to find the right ship, that was in a really interesting state of disassembly. And these tankers are very unusual boats. It just looked weird, like some kind of a spaceship. It takes workers a long time to break it down. And then they have to wait for the tide to be right so they can pull the pieces ashore. They have big winches and boats that they use to get the stuff ashore."
paragraphs.zh: 他毫不气馁，用无人机勘察并拍摄了恰特马港以北的整个海岸线，寻找一艘能够拍出特别醒目照片的船。他最终选中了液化天然气油轮。“对我来说，关键是找到合适的船，它正处于一种非常有趣的拆解状态。这些油轮是非常特殊的船。它看上去很奇怪，就像某种宇宙飞船。工人们需要很长时间才能将其拆解。然后他们必须等到潮水合适，才能把船的零件拉到岸上。他们有大型绞车和船只用来把这些东西运上岸。”

paragraphs.en: He was able to convince the owner of the tanker to allow him to photograph it. The timing of the drone photo was crucial. Steinmetz wanted to capture the vessel at low tide, when the surrounding mudflats were exposed and workers could be seen moving around its enormous hull. Their tiny figures would look like ants, giving viewers a sense of the ship's mammoth scale. He spent several days photographing the vessel, returning as the tides shifted and the workers continued to take the ship apart for scrap metal.
paragraphs.zh: 他能够说服油轮的船主允许他拍摄它。无人机拍摄的时间至关重要。斯坦梅茨希望在退潮时拍摄这艘船，那时候周围的泥滩暴露出来，工人们可以被看到在巨大的船体周围移动。他们渺小的身影看起来就像蚂蚁一样，让观众感受到船的庞大规模。他花了好几天时间拍摄这艘船，随着潮汐变化回到现场，工人们继续拆解船体以回收废金属。

articles.title: Israel is in a political deadlock. What comes next?
articles.dek: TEL AVIV, Israel — Israel's election has produced a political deadlock, leaving neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, with a clear path to forming a…

paragraphs.en: TEL AVIV, Israel — Israel's election has produced a political deadlock, leaving neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, with a clear path to forming a government.
paragraphs.zh: 以色列特拉维夫--以色列大选造成了政治僵局，本雅明·内塔尼亚胡总理和他的主要挑战者加迪·艾森科特都没有走上组建政府的明确道路。

paragraphs.en: The final results announced Friday give opposition parties more seats than Netanyahu's right-wing bloc. But Eisenkot, a center-right former military chief of staff, cannot reach a governing majority without the support of predominantly Arab parties — an option Eisenkot's allies repeatedly ruled out during the campaign.
paragraphs.zh: 周五公布的最终结果使反对党比内塔尼亚胡的右翼集团获得更多席位。但是，如果没有主要是阿拉伯政党的支持，中右翼的前军事参谋长艾森科特就无法获得执政党的多数席位—艾森科特的盟友在竞选期间一再排除了这一选择。

paragraphs.en: Netanyahu's Likud party received the most votes — winning 27 seats — but his bloc lost the majority it had before the election. The coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties that supported his government won a combined 53 seats. At least 61 seats are needed for a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset.
paragraphs.zh: 内塔尼亚胡的利库德集团获得了最多的选票，赢得了27个席位，但他的集团失去了选举前的多数席位。支持他的政府的右翼、极右翼和极端东正教政党联盟共赢得了53个席位。在以色列120个席位的议会（即以色列议会）中，至少需要61个席位才能获得多数席位。

paragraphs.en: Here is what happens next and the possible paths to a new Israeli government.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是接下来会发生什么，以及通往以色列新政府的可能途径。

paragraphs.en: In the next few days, Israel's president will consult with the leaders of every party elected to parliament. Each party will recommend the party leader it believes should be given the first opportunity to form a coalition.
paragraphs.zh: 在接下来的几天里，以色列总统将与当选议会的每个政党的领导人进行磋商。每个政党都会推荐它认为应该第一次有机会组成联盟的政党领导人。

paragraphs.en: The president is not required to choose the leader of the largest party. Instead, the president selects the candidate considered most likely to assemble a governing coalition.
paragraphs.zh: 总统不需要选择最大政党的领导人。相反，总统选择最有可能组建执政联盟的候选人。

paragraphs.en: That candidate is given 28 days to secure the support of at least 61 lawmakers. The president may grant an extension of up to 14 days. If the effort fails, the president can give another candidate an opportunity to form a government.
paragraphs.zh: 该候选人有28天的时间获得至少61名立法者的支持。总统可以批准最多14天的延期。如果这一努力失败，总统可以给另一位候选人组建政府的机会。

paragraphs.en: The process could take weeks, or months, or end without anyone assembling a majority.
paragraphs.zh: 这个过程可能需要数周或数月，或者在没有人占多数的情况下结束。

paragraphs.en: Who is most likely to get the first opportunity to form a coalition?
paragraphs.zh: 谁最有可能获得组建联盟的第一个机会？

articles.title: Hackers steal over $6 billion from crypto exchange Binance in staggering heist
articles.dek: More than $6 billion worth of cryptocurrencies were stolen from Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange. It's the biggest cyber heist ever — and many suspect North Korea may be behind it.

paragraphs.en: More than $6 billion worth of cryptocurrencies were stolen from Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange. It's the biggest cyber heist ever — and many suspect North Korea may be behind it.
paragraphs.zh: 全球最大的加密货币交易所币安（ Binance ）价值超过60 $十亿的加密货币被盗。这是有史以来规模最大的网络抢劫，许多人怀疑朝鲜可能是幕后黑手。

paragraphs.en: It is the biggest cyber heist in history. Hackers were able to steal over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance, the biggest crypto exchange in the world. Among those likely affected was everyone from investment funds to everyday investors who trade digital currencies like Bitcoin in the exchange. For more on this developing story, I am joined by NPR senior business editor Rafael Nam. Hey, Rafael.
paragraphs.zh: 这是有史以来规模最大的网络抢劫案。黑客能够从世界上最大的加密货币交易所Binance窃取价值超过60 $十亿的加密货币。可能受到影响的人包括从投资基金到在交易所交易比特币等数字货币的日常投资者。关于这个发展中的故事的更多信息， NPR高级商业编辑Rafael Nam也加入了我的行列。嘿，拉斐尔。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: So if you took $6 billion out of a bank in bags, you would need quite a lot of bags to get it out. I mean, this is a staggering amount of money. What happened?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW ：所以，如果你从银行拿出60亿美元的袋子，你需要很多袋子才能把它拿出来。我的意思是，这是一笔惊人的钱，发生了什么？

paragraphs.en: NAM: I know. And it's such a fascinating story, honestly. So according to researchers, the heist happened in late afternoon, and the entire thing only took about 20 minutes - 20 minutes for the bulk of the $6 billion to be stolen.
paragraphs.zh: 南：我知道，老实说，这是一个非常有趣的故事。因此，根据研究人员的说法，抢劫发生在下午晚些时候，整个过程只花了大约20分钟- 20分钟，大部分60亿美元的$被盗。

paragraphs.en: Now, Binance and researchers are still trying to figure out exactly how it happened. But the gist of it is that the hackers were able to effectively bypass all kinds of security systems and hack into the trading accounts that people held at this crypto exchange. So this is how Ari Redbord, who's the global head of policy at TRM Labs, a major crypto research firm, put it.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，币安和研究人员仍在试图弄清楚它是如何发生的。但其要点是，黑客能够有效地绕过各种安全系统，侵入人们在这个加密交易所持有的交易账户。这就是大型加密研究公司TRM Labs的全球政策主管Ari Redbord所说的。

paragraphs.en: ARI REDBORD: What happened last night is the largest bank robbery in human history. Imagine a world where someone could walk into a bank and walk out with $6.36 billion in stolen funds and then move those funds at the speed of the internet.
paragraphs.zh: ARI REDBORD ：昨晚发生的事情是人类历史上最大的银行抢劫案。想象一下这样一个世界：有人走进银行，带着63.6亿美元的被盗资金走出去，然后以互联网的速度转移这些资金。

paragraphs.en: NAM: I mean, imagine. And TRM and other researchers I talked to say they are very confident that all fingers point to the state of North Korea.
paragraphs.zh: NAM ：我的意思是，想象一下。TRM和我采访过的其他研究人员表示，他们非常有信心，所有人都指向朝鲜的状态。

paragraphs.en: NAM: Now, Redbord says he's sure it's North Korea because they have a history of cyberattacks, and this heist was really well planned and executed.
paragraphs.zh: NAM ：现在， Redbord说他确信这是朝鲜，因为他们有网络攻击的历史，这次抢劫非常精心策划和执行。

articles.title: Nearly 2 out of 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots, new research shows
articles.dek: Artificial intelligence chatbots are increasingly becoming a regular part of life for American youth. Two new surveys show that nearly two-thirds of tweens and teens use AI chatbots. While most…

paragraphs.en: Artificial intelligence chatbots are increasingly becoming a regular part of life for American youth. Two new surveys show that nearly two-thirds of tweens and teens use AI chatbots. While most kids use the technology for help with school work, and for companionship and emotional support, certain uses were linked with worse mental health symptoms.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能聊天机器人正日益成为美国年轻人日常生活的一部分。两项新的调查显示，近三分之二的青少年使用人工智能聊天机器人。虽然大多数孩子使用这项技术来帮助学校工作，以及友谊和情感支持，但某些用途与更严重的心理健康症状有关。

paragraphs.en: One survey, done by the online safety advocacy group, Common Sense Media, found that AI use starts early – years before kids hit the minimum age of 13 on most popular chatbots. Nearly half 9-to-12-year-olds have used an AI chatbot or companion. By the time kids are 13 years old, nearly three-quarters of them have used chatbots.
paragraphs.zh: 由在线安全倡导组织Common Sense Media进行的一项调查发现，人工智能的使用始于早期，即儿童在最受欢迎的聊天机器人上达到13岁的最低年龄之前几年。将近一半的9至12岁儿童使用过人工智能聊天机器人或伴侣。到孩子13岁时，近四分之三的孩子使用过聊天机器人。

paragraphs.en: The other survey, done by the mental health advocacy group JED Foundation, found that 90% of the 5,500 9-to-17-year-olds in schools across the country have used an AI chatbot. Nearly two-thirds use it both for schoolwork and as companions, or when they are stressed, lonely, anxious or overwhelmed.
paragraphs.zh: 另一项由心理健康倡导组织JED基金会进行的调查发现，全国学校中5500名9至17岁的青少年中，90%的人使用过人工智能聊天机器人。近三分之二的人将其用于完成学校作业、陪伴学习，或在感到压力、孤独、焦虑或不知所措时使用。

paragraphs.en: The findings are "remarkable" in showing how dramatically AI use by children and teens has changed in a short time, says developmental psychologist Anne Maheux at the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, who wasn't involved in the surveys.
paragraphs.zh: 北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校（ University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill ）的发展心理学家安妮·马赫（ Anne Maheux ）说，这一发现“引人注目”地表明，儿童和青少年使用人工智能的情况在短时间内发生了巨大变化。

paragraphs.en: "It seems like just a few years ago, no one was using" the technology, she says. "And now it seems like roughly the same number of kids using it for homework are using it to get emotional support or help with coping."
paragraphs.zh: 她说： “几年前，似乎没有人使用这项技术。” “现在看来，大约有相同数量的孩子用它来做作业，以获得情感支持或帮助应对。”

paragraphs.en: "I use it to make myself practice sample questions – sample test questions that I will answer with my own work," says 15-year-old Arjun Sharda, in Round Rock, Texas. "I use it to understand concepts outside of the classroom."
paragraphs.zh: 15岁的Arjun Sharda在德克萨斯州的Round Rock说： “我用它来练习样题--我将用自己的作品回答的样题。” “我用它来理解课堂之外的概念。”

paragraphs.en: He uses both OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini, he says, although he prefers the latter lately.

articles.title: Trump says he's ending restrictions on climate-warming methane from oil drilling
articles.dek: BILLINGS, Mont. — President Donald Trump said Tuesday that his administration is "terminating" a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling.

paragraphs.en: BILLINGS, Mont. — President Donald Trump said Tuesday that his administration is "terminating" a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling.
paragraphs.zh: 蒙大拿州比林斯——总统唐纳德·特朗普周二表示，他的政府正在“终止”拜登时期的一项规则，该规则旨在减少石油和天然气钻探产生的温室气体甲烷排放。

paragraphs.en: Trump said during a campaign rally in Texas that the change would save companies and consumers billions of dollars and unlock 210 million barrels of oil. That's equivalent to about 10 days of U.S. petroleum consumption.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普在德克萨斯州的一次竞选集会上表示，这一变化将为公司和消费者节省数十亿美元，并释放出2.1亿桶石油。这相当于美国约10天的石油消耗量。

paragraphs.en: The move aims to encourage more domestic drilling as Trump faces criticism over high fuel prices amid the war in Iran.
paragraphs.zh: 此举旨在鼓励更多的国内钻探，因为特朗普在伊朗战争期间面临有关高油价的批评。

paragraphs.en: Methane is responsible for about a third of planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions, scientists estimate.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家估计，甲烷约占导致地球变暖的温室气体排放的三分之一。

paragraphs.en: Cuts in methane emissions have emerged in recent years as a global priority to slow the rate of climate change. Oil and gas operations are the largest industrial source of methane, which is the main component in natural gas and far more potent to the atmosphere than carbon dioxide in the short term.
paragraphs.zh: 近年来，减少甲烷排放已成为全球的优先事项，以减缓气候变化的速度。石油和天然气作业是最大的工业甲烷来源，甲烷是天然气的主要成分，在短期内对大气的影响远比二氧化碳更强。

paragraphs.en: The invisible gas leaks from equipment and is released into the atmosphere or burned off as a waste product by oil drillers.
paragraphs.zh: 这种看不见的气体从设备中泄漏，并被释放到大气中，或被石油钻探工作为废弃物燃烧掉。

paragraphs.en: Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin previewed the changes last month, saying they would eliminate the agency's "Super Emitter Program" that requires companies to investigate and repair major methane releases from oil and natural gas facilities. The agency would also set less restrictive standards for small oil and gas wells.
paragraphs.zh: 环境保护局局长李·泽尔丁上个月预览了这些变化，他表示，这些变化将取消该机构的“超级排放者计划”，该计划要求公司调查并修复油气设施的大量甲烷泄漏。该机构还将为小型油气井设定较少限制的标准。

paragraphs.en: Trump said during Tuesday's rally in Lubbock for Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton that Biden's plan "crushed the small operators" with crippling regulations.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普在周二为德克萨斯州共和党参议员候选人肯·帕克斯顿在拉伯克举行的集会上表示，拜登的计划“用压垮性的法规摧毁了小型运营商”。

articles.title: Here's what it's like to live in Salem, Mass., during the Halloween tourism season
articles.dek: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with reporter Megan Johnson, who wrote about what it's like to live in Salem, Mass. — famous for the Salem Witch Trials — during Halloween tourism season.

paragraphs.en: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with reporter Megan Johnson, who wrote about what it's like to live in Salem, Mass. — famous for the Salem Witch Trials — during Halloween tourism season.
paragraphs.zh: NPR的斯科特·德特罗与记者梅根·约翰逊交谈，约翰逊曾撰文描述在马萨诸塞州塞勒姆生活的感受——那里以塞勒姆女巫审判闻名——正值万圣节旅游季节。

paragraphs.en: It is a pretty good time to be a witch in Salem, Massachusetts, certainly compared to 1692, when dozens of witchcraft claims led to 19 public executions plus other deaths in prison. This was, of course, the Salem witch trials. Over 300 years later, the story is why a different of mass hysteria takes over Salem every fall. The small city just north of Boston has become enormously popular for Halloween tourists in October. Reporter Megan Johnson has written about what that is like for boston.com and is with us now. Welcome.
paragraphs.zh: 现在在马萨诸塞州的塞勒姆当一名女巫是相当不错的时光，当然，相比1692年，当时数十起巫术指控导致19人被公开处决，以及其他人在狱中死亡。当然，那就是塞勒姆女巫审判。三百多年后，这个故事解释了为什么每年秋天不同的集体歇斯底里会席卷塞勒姆。这个位于波士顿北部的小城市在十月已成为万圣节游客的极受欢迎的目的地。记者梅根·约翰逊曾为boston.com撰写过相关报道，现在她也在我们这里。欢迎你。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: Tell me what the draw is. I mean, it makes sense. This historic town tied to witch trials - makes sense that it would be a Halloween destination. But, like, what is there to do? Say you're thinking of driving up to Salem to check it out in October. What's available?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：告诉我吸引人的是什么。我的意思是，这很有道理。这个与女巫审判有关的历史小镇——作为万圣节目的地很合理。但是，有什么好玩的呢？假设你打算十月份开车去塞勒姆看看。那边有什么可做的事情？

paragraphs.en: JOHNSON: There is so much to do. Besides the fact that it is just an absolutely stunning town that is the epitome of autumn when the weather changes, people love the historic aspect, so they want to go to the Salem Witch Museum, the House of Seven Gables, the nun on stilts, which is one of the very common buskers on the street. There's people in costume all the time. It's a big bachelorette trip draw.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰逊：有太多事情可以做。此外，这个小镇本身就非常迷人，当天气转凉时，它是秋天的典型代表。人们喜欢它的历史方面，所以他们想去塞勒姆女巫博物馆、七尖屋、踩高跷的修女，这些都是街上很常见的表演者。街上总是有人穿着服装。这是一个吸引大型单身派对旅行的地方。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: Has all of this grown in recent years? Like, and is there...
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：这些在近些年都有增长吗？比如说，是否有……

paragraphs.en: JOHNSON: So it has grown tremendously in recent years, pretty across the board, every resident has said. And a lot of them really attribute that to social media - Instagram, social media influencers who descend upon the city and want to caption amazing content. And because there's so much of that content out there, that brings such a draw of visitors who see it and want to participate in it, too.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰逊：所以近年来它增长非常迅猛，几乎各方面都是如此，每位居民都这么说过。而且很多人真的将这种增长归因于社交媒体——Instagram、社交媒体影响者们来到这座城市，希望为精彩的内容加上说明。由于有那么多这样的内容，这吸引了大量的游客，他们看到后也想参与其中。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: So let's set the scene. It's about 45,000 people live in Salem, and - what? - a million people visit in October. What is that like on a fall Saturday?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：那我们来设定一下场景。塞勒姆大约有45,000人居住，而——什么？——每年十月有一百万人来访。秋天的一个星期六会是怎样的情景？

paragraphs.en: JOHNSON: The No. 1 complaint that people have is that it's nonstop traffic, and there's nowhere to park, and that comes from residents and visitors. But there's also just a constant onslaught of people in the streets, which often get shut down as an attempt to get rid of some of the traffic. But moving around, navigating the streets is pretty crazy.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰逊：人们抱怨最多的是交通不断，而且没有地方停车，这些抱怨来自居民和游客。但街上也有源源不断的人群，这些街道经常因为试图减少一些交通而被封闭。不过在街上移动、穿行还是相当疯狂的。

articles.title: US and Japan agree to establish a Japanese facility for joint missile production
articles.dek: CEBU, Philippines — The United States and Japan have agreed to establish a Japanese facility for the joint production of advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles, the Japanese defense chief said.

paragraphs.en: CEBU, Philippines — The United States and Japan have agreed to establish a Japanese facility for the joint production of advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles, the Japanese defense chief said.
paragraphs.zh: 菲律宾宿务——日本防卫负责人表示，美国和日本已同意建立一个用于联合生产先进中程空对空导弹的日本设施。

paragraphs.en: It is the latest move by the allies, which have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.
paragraphs.zh: 这是盟友的最新举动，他们已多次对中国在亚洲日益增长的自信表示担忧。

paragraphs.en: Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi made the announcement in a news conference Wednesday night in the central Philippine province of Cebu, where he met U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of an annual meeting of Southeast Asian defense chiefs and their major Asian and Western counterparts.
paragraphs.zh: 日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎在周三晚上于菲律宾中部宿务省举行的新闻发布会上宣布此消息，他在那里在东南亚防长及其主要亚洲和西方同行年度会议的间隙会见了美国国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯。

paragraphs.en: Koizumi raised concern Thursday about China's increasing naval activity in southwestern Japan. He said that three Chinese destroyers and a coast guard ship together crossed the Osumi Strait south of the southern main island of Kyushu and headed east to the Pacific Ocean this week. It was the first such fleet configuration his ministry has spotted, he said.
paragraphs.zh: 小泉周四对中国在日本西南部日益增加的海军活动表示关注。他说，本周有三艘中国驱逐舰和一艘海警船一起穿过九州南部主岛以南的大隅海峡，向东驶向太平洋。他表示，这是他所在部门首次发现这样的舰队配置。

paragraphs.en: Koizumi said he cited the incident as "an example illustrating the challenging security environment in the region" in his remark at a session Thursday. His ministry will keep watching the Chinese activity with high level of interest, he said. Japan has been accelerating military buildup in southwestern Japan to deter China.
paragraphs.zh: 小泉在周四的一个会议上表示，他引用这一事件是“作为说明该地区安全环境严峻的一个例子”。他表示，政府将以高度关注继续观察中国的活动。日本一直在加速加强西南日本的军事建设，以威慑中国。

paragraphs.en: The annual meetings aim to avert a major regional conflict and strengthen defense cooperation. On the sidelines of the meetings, however, the U.S. and China and their allies have often traded criticisms.
paragraphs.zh: 年度会议旨在避免重大地区冲突并加强防务合作。然而，在会议期间，美国和中国及其盟友经常互相批评。

paragraphs.en: The missiles that will be produced as part of a joint effort called "Operation Supercharge" are essential for the F-35 fighter jets, Koizumi said. The two sides agreed to build a final assembly and inspection plant for the Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile, or AMRAAM, in Japan, he said. The U.S.-made F-35s are one of the world's most advanced aircraft and are also used by the Japanese military.
paragraphs.zh: 小泉表示，作为名为“超级充能行动”的联合努力一部分将生产的导弹对于F-35战斗机至关重要。他说，双方同意在日本建造一座先进中程空对空导弹（AMRAAM）的最终装配和检查工厂。美国制造的F-35是世界上最先进的飞机之一，也被日本军方使用。

paragraphs.en: During his brief meeting with Hegseth in Cebu, Koizumi said he "shared a sense of crisis … regarding the increasingly severe regional situation and we agreed to strengthen the deterrence and response capabilities of the Japan-U.S. alliance with greater speed and intensity than ever before."
paragraphs.zh: 在他与赫格塞斯在宿务的简短会面中，小泉表示，他“对日益严峻的地区局势有共同的危机感……我们同意比以往任何时候都更快、更强地加强日美联盟的威慑和应对能力。”

articles.title: With days to go before the midterms, data shows the U.S. economy is doing well
articles.dek: The U.S. economy grew faster in the summer compared to the spring, driven by consumer spending as well as investments in AI.

paragraphs.en: The U.S. economy grew faster in the summer compared to the spring, driven by consumer spending as well as investments in AI.
paragraphs.zh: 美国经济在夏季的增长速度比春季更快，这得益于消费者支出以及对人工智能的投资。

paragraphs.en: Gross domestic product, which broadly measures economic activity, grew at an annual rate of 3.4% July through September, according to a report from the Commerce Department released Thursday. The previous quarter GDP grew at a 2.2% annual pace.
paragraphs.zh: 根据商务部周四发布的一份报告，从七月到九月，广泛衡量经济活动的国内生产总值以3.4%的年增长率增长。上一季度国内生产总值的年增长速度为2.2%。

paragraphs.en: A big driver for GDP growth in the third quarter was the strong investments from AI companies, which continue to build out data centers and spend big money in developing the technology.
paragraphs.zh: 第三季度 GDP 增长的一个重要驱动力是人工智能公司的强劲投资，这些公司继续建设数据中心，并在技术开发上投入大量资金。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, consumer spending was another of the big drivers of GDP growth, led in part by higher-income Americans who are better able to withstand stubbornly high inflation.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，消费者支出是国内生产总值增长的另一个重要推动力，部分原因是高收入的美国人能够更好地应对持续高企的通货膨胀。

paragraphs.en: The sturdy GDP data comes just days before the midterm elections, with many Americans saying they feel gloomy about the economy as inflation jacks up the costs of many day-to-day necessities, while the ongoing conflict with Iran drives up energy costs like gasoline.
paragraphs.zh: 坚挺的国内生产总值数据发布就在中期选举前几天，许多美国人表示他们对经济感到悲观，因为通货膨胀推高了许多日常必需品的成本，而与伊朗的持续冲突又推高了汽油等能源成本。

paragraphs.en: Although consumer spending has been growing steadily, it has not spread out evenly across households, with lower-income Americans struggling more than high-earners. Wage growth has also fallen behind inflation, further squeezing many Americans.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管消费者支出一直在稳步增长，但它在各家庭之间的分布并不均匀，低收入美国人的困难比高收入者更多。工资增长也落后于通货膨胀，进一步压缩了许多美国人的生活空间。

paragraphs.en: Siri Steven, a manager at a resale store in Decorah, Iowa, says she and her husband are putting off fixing up their more than 130-year-old house.
paragraphs.zh: 爱荷华州德科拉一家转售店的经理Siri Steven说，她和她的丈夫正在推迟修缮他们那座已有130多年历史的房子。

paragraphs.en: "We barely go out to eat now," Steven said. "I really have to be mindful of our budget and make sure that we can pay all our bills and not overdraft."
paragraphs.zh: “我们现在几乎不出去吃饭了，”史蒂文说。“我真的必须注意我们的预算，确保我们能支付所有账单，避免透支。”

articles.title: Who benefits when massive AI data centers come to town?
articles.dek: The battle over data centers is hitting the ballot box. Brookings scholar Darrell West talks about how the backlash against the AI boom, flock cameras and tech companies is crossing party lines.

paragraphs.en: The battle over data centers is hitting the ballot box. Brookings scholar Darrell West talks about how the backlash against the AI boom, flock cameras and tech companies is crossing party lines.
paragraphs.zh: 围绕数据中心的争斗正影响到投票箱。布鲁金斯学者达雷尔·韦斯特谈到，对人工智能热潮、聚众摄像头和科技公司的反弹正跨越党派界限。

paragraphs.en: This is FRESH AIR. I'm Tonya Mosley. The AI boom has a problem. It has to be built somewhere, and to power it, tech companies are building massive data centers. They need land, enormous amounts of electricity, and in many cases, water. In exchange, they promise jobs and community investment. But people who live in these communities are demanding to know, what's this going to cost us? There's also another question, who gets to decide? In communities from Wisconsin to Louisiana, residents say local officials are negotiating data center deals without their input.
paragraphs.zh: 这里是《清新空气》。我是托尼娅·莫斯利。人工智能热潮存在一个问题。它必须在某个地方建造，而为了为其提供动力，科技公司正在建设庞大的数据中心。他们需要土地、大量的电力，并且在很多情况下，还需要水资源。作为交换，他们承诺提供就业机会和社区投资。但住在这些社区的人们要求知道，这将花费我们什么代价？还有另一个问题，谁有权决定？从威斯康星到路易斯安那的社区，居民们表示，当地官员在未经他们参与的情况下，正在协商数据中心的交易。

paragraphs.en: This midterm election, voters in more than 40 cities and towns across eight states will decide ballot measures on data center bans, moratoriums and requirements that residents get a vote before one is built. And Democrats and Republicans are going after their opponents for what used to be a bragging right, the ability to bring billions of dollars in investment to town. My guest is Darrell West, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution. He and his colleague, Nicol Turner Lee, write about the backlash against AI data centers and how these local fights are becoming part of something much bigger, a challenge to the enormous power of the tech industry and who gets to decide what our future looks like. And, Darrell West, welcome to FRESH AIR.
paragraphs.zh: 在这次中期选举中，来自八个州的40多个城市和城镇的选民将决定关于数据中心禁止、暂停建设以及居民在数据中心建成前必须投票表决的选票措施。民主党人和共和党人现在相互攻击对手，而批评的焦点曾经是他们的骄傲所在——能够为城镇带来数十亿美元的投资。我的嘉宾是布鲁金斯学会的高级研究员达雷尔·韦斯特。他和同事尼科尔·特纳·李撰文讨论了针对人工智能数据中心的反弹，以及这些地方斗争如何成为更大事物的一部分——对科技行业巨大力量的挑战，以及谁来决定我们的未来会是什么样子。达雷尔·韦斯特，欢迎来到《新鲜空气》节目。

paragraphs.en: MOSLEY: Well, I actually want to start with a couple of political ads. And the first one is from Ohio, where Democrat Sherrod Brown is challenging Republican Senator Jon Husted. And Brown accuses Husted of aggressively courting data centers and backing corporate tax breaks while residents face rising electricity bills. Let's listen.
paragraphs.zh: 莫斯利：好吧，我实际上想从几条政治广告开始。第一条来自俄亥俄州，民主党人谢罗德·布朗正在挑战共和党参议员乔恩·赫斯特。布朗指责赫斯特积极争取数据中心，并支持企业减税，而居民则面临不断上涨的电费账单。让我们来听听。

paragraphs.en: UNIDENTIFIED NARRATOR #1: He's been called the face of data centers in Ohio. Why? Because Jon Husted spent years aggressively recruiting data centers to the state, cutting sweetheart tax deals and fast-tracking approvals while ordinary residents watch their electricity bills explode.
paragraphs.zh: 未确认叙述者 #1：他被称为俄亥俄州数据中心的代言人。为什么？因为Jon Husted花了多年时间积极招揽数据中心落户该州，提供优惠税收协议并加快审批流程，而普通居民却眼睁睁看着自己的电费飙升。

articles.title: Even birds get jet lagged, study shows
articles.dek: New research shows that humans are not the only species to get jet lag: Some birds appear to experience it too.

paragraphs.en: New research shows that humans are not the only species to get jet lag: Some birds appear to experience it too.
paragraphs.zh: 新的研究表明，人类并不是唯一会经历时差反应的物种：一些鸟类似乎也会经历时差反应。

paragraphs.en: A study published in the journal Science found that a type of seabird known as the Manx shearwater appears to become slightly disoriented during long flights across the Atlantic Ocean. That disorientation, the authors say, is due to the bird's internal clock falling out of sync with the sun's position in the sky.
paragraphs.zh: 发表在《科学》杂志上的一项研究发现，一种被称为曼岛剪尾鸥的海鸟在穿越大西洋的长途飞行中似乎会稍微迷失方向。作者表示，这种迷失方向是由于鸟类的生物钟与太阳在天空中的位置不同步所导致的。

paragraphs.en: Manx shearwaters are a common bird in the British Isles. They look a little like seagulls, but "they're actually very closely related to an albatross," said Patrick Lewin, a behavioral ecologist at the University of Oxford.
paragraphs.zh: 曼岛海燕是英伦群岛常见的鸟类。它们看起来有点像海鸥，但“它们实际上与信天翁关系非常密切，”牛津大学行为生态学家帕特里克·卢因说。

paragraphs.en: Shearwaters mate for life, and when they breed, a couple lays just one egg.
paragraphs.zh: 海燕终生配偶，当它们繁殖时，一对只会下一个蛋。

paragraphs.en: Then they take turns incubating it: "One partner will sit on the egg nonstop while the other one goes out to sea," Lewin said.
paragraphs.zh: 然后它们轮流孵蛋：“一只伴侣会一直坐在蛋上，而另一只则出海，”卢因说道。

paragraphs.en: For up to two weeks the hunting partners scour the North Atlantic for fish and squid, often travelling hundreds of miles from their nests.
paragraphs.zh: 在长达两周的时间里，捕猎伙伴在北大西洋寻找鱼类和鱿鱼，常常从它们的巢穴出发，行程达数百英里。

paragraphs.en: Once these birds' bellies are full "they absolutely bomb it back to their colony," Lewin said. Often they make the long journey home in just a day or so.
paragraphs.zh: Lewin 说，一旦这些鸟的肚子吃饱了，它们就会“立即飞回它们的巢穴”。它们通常只需一天左右就能完成漫长的回家旅程。

paragraphs.en: Which raised an interesting question: Do Manx shearwaters feel jet lag (or perhaps more aptly, flap lag)?
paragraphs.zh: 这就引出了一个有趣的问题：马恩岛剪尾海燕会感到时差反应（或者更恰当地说，拍翅疲劳）吗？

paragraphs.en: To see if these little birds really did feel the effects of flying through time zones like humans do, Lewin used a remarkable tool – for 20 years, his colleagues had been tagging birds with GPS trackers and collecting data on their flights out to the Atlantic and back.
paragraphs.zh: 为了看看这些小鸟是否真的像人类一样感受到穿越时区的影响，刘文使用了一种非凡的工具——在过去20年里，他的同事们一直在给鸟类装上GPS追踪器，并收集它们往返大西洋的飞行数据。

articles.title: Patrick Stewart, a perceptive patriarch in 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men,' dies at 86
articles.dek: Sir Patrick Stewart's most famous characters tackled concepts such as honor, morality and courage. He played Professor X in the X-Men franchise and Jean-Luc Picard, captain of the starship USS…

paragraphs.en: Sir Patrick Stewart's most famous characters tackled concepts such as honor, morality and courage. He played Professor X in the X-Men franchise and Jean-Luc Picard, captain of the starship USS Enterprise, on the show Star Trek: The Next Generation and its later spinoff, Picard.
paragraphs.zh: 帕特里克·斯图尔特爵士最著名的角色探讨了荣誉、道德和勇气等概念。他在《X 战警》系列中饰演了X教授，在电视剧《星际迷航：下一代》及其后来的衍生剧《皮卡德》中饰演了星舰企业号的船长让-卢克·皮卡尔。

paragraphs.en: Stewart died Wednesday at 86. A post on his Facebook and Instagram pages said he died at home in Los Angeles after a "brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia."
paragraphs.zh: 斯图尔特于周三去世，享年86岁。他的Facebook和Instagram页面上的一则帖子称，他在洛杉矶的家中去世，死因是在经历了“与阿尔茨海默病和路易体痴呆症的短暂而深刻的旅程”之后。

paragraphs.en: Although he was beloved for playing compassionate father figures who united families of misfits, Stewart's own upbringing in Yorkshire, England, was harsh. He remembered his father as alcoholic and abusive. He found solace in school and, eventually, in Shakespeare. He joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966 and debuted on Broadway in 1970 in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管他因扮演充满同情心、能够团结各种怪人家庭的父亲角色而受到喜爱，但斯图尔特自己在英国约克郡的成长经历却十分艰难。他记得自己的父亲酗酒且虐待人。他在学校找到了慰藉，最终在莎士比亚的作品中找到了安慰。他于1966年加入皇家莎士比亚剧团，并于1970年在百老汇的《仲夏夜之梦》中首次登台演出。

paragraphs.en: "To stand in the middle of an empty stage in an empty theater and feel that I was at home was everything," he told NPR in 2023. "But it took a while for me to get there."
paragraphs.zh: 他在2023年告诉NPR：“站在一座空剧院的空舞台中央，感受到自己仿佛在家里，这就是一切。但我花了一段时间才达到那个状态。”

paragraphs.en: Stewart played alongside some of the best Shakespeareans of his time, including Judi Dench and Ian McKellen. He was lecturing on Shakespeare at UCLA when his name came up for the lead in a new series of Star Trek.
paragraphs.zh: 斯图尔特与他那个时代的一些最优秀的莎士比亚演员一起演出，包括朱迪·丹奇和伊恩·麦克莱恩。当他在加州大学洛杉矶分校讲授莎士比亚时，他的名字被提名为新一季《星际迷航》的主角。

paragraphs.en: "Don't do this, Patrick," he remembered McKellen advising him. "You're a very good stage actor. That's where you ought to be. Don't do it."
paragraphs.zh: “别这么做，帕特里克，”他记得麦克凯伦曾劝告他。“你是个非常好的舞台演员。你应该待在舞台上。别做这件事。”

paragraphs.en: But Stewart's agent had reassured him that the show was unlikely to make it past the first season. As the actor recalled to NPR, he was encouraged to take what he believed to be a quick and easy job. "'Do six months' work. Make some money for the first time in your life and get well known. Get a suntan, and go home.' And I thought, 'Yeah, that doesn't sound too bad. I could live with that.'"
paragraphs.zh: 但斯图尔特的经纪人向他保证，这部剧不太可能超过第一季。正如这位演员向NPR回忆的那样，他被鼓励去接他认为是一个快速且轻松的工作。‘干六个月的活。第一次赚钱并让自己出名。晒晒太阳，然后回家。’我当时心想，‘是啊，这听起来还不错。我能接受这个。’

paragraphs.en: But Star Trek: The Next Generation was a tremendous hit. It aired for seven seasons, from 1987 to 1994. Stewart was embraced by fans, who adored the character's penchant for Earl Grey tea and cool-headed leadership, with such signature phrases as "Engage!" and "Make it so!"
paragraphs.zh: 但是《星际迷航：下一代》取得了巨大的成功。它从1987年播出到1994年，共播出七季。斯图尔特受到了粉丝的喜爱，粉丝们喜爱这个角色对伯爵茶的偏爱以及冷静的领导风格，以及他标志性的台词，如“出发！”和“照办！”

articles.title: Brazilian political drama unfolds as defeated Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami
articles.dek: Defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family have arrived in the U.S. after Brazilian authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. He is facing multiple investigations in…

paragraphs.en: Defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family have arrived in the U.S. after Brazilian authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. He is facing multiple investigations in Brazil.
paragraphs.zh: 落选总统候选人弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗及其家人已抵达美国，此前巴西当局曾命令他交出护照。他在巴西面临多项调查。

paragraphs.en: This morning, Brazilians were glued to their screens watching a private plane land at an airport in Miami, Florida. Moments later, the man who had just lost Brazil's presidential election, Flávio Bolsonaro, stepped out onto the tarmac. His arrival capped three days of political drama since his stunning defeat to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. NPR South America correspondent Carrie Kahn is on the line now. Hey, Carrie.
paragraphs.zh: 今天早上，巴西人紧盯着屏幕，观看一架私人飞机降落在佛罗里达州迈阿密的一座机场。片刻之后，刚刚在巴西总统选举中失利的弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗走出了停机坪。他的到来为自他在选举中意外败给现任总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦以来的三天政治戏剧画上句号。NPR南美记者凯莉·卡恩现在在线。嗨，凯莉。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: So, Carrie, I want to make sure I understand this correctly. Bolsonaro lost Sunday's election, and by Wednesday, he was in the U.S.?
paragraphs.zh: 萨默斯：所以，凯莉，我想确认我理解正确。博尔索纳罗在周日的选举中失败了，而到了周三，他已经在美国了？

paragraphs.en: KAHN: Yes, it's been a wild ride the past three days. On Sunday, he refused to concede the election and said he would petition to annul the results. The next day, his party did accept the results. And in a video, Bolsonaro seemed to back down a bit but added that federal police demanded his passport after he was visiting his father, who is under house arrest for attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula four years ago. By Tuesday - yesterday - rumors were flying that Bolsonaro had fled Brazil, and today he arrived in Miami and then later put out a statement first declaring himself as, quote, "the true elected president of Brazil." Then a bit later, he posted a new statement downgrading himself to the true elected leader of Brazil. He compared himself to liberation figures like Charles de Gaulle and María Corina Machado of Venezuela, amongst others.
paragraphs.zh: KAHN：是的，过去三天真是经历了一场疯狂的旅程。周日，他拒绝承认选举结果，并表示将申请撤销选举结果。第二天，他的政党接受了选举结果。在一段视频中，博尔索纳罗似乎有所退让，但他补充说，联邦警察在他探望父亲时要求上交护照，他的父亲因四年前试图推翻自己输给卢拉的选举而被软禁。到了周二——也就是昨天——有传闻称博尔索纳罗已经逃离巴西，而今天他抵达迈阿密，随后发表声明，首先自称为“巴西真正当选总统”。过了一会儿，他又发布了一份新声明，将自己降格为巴西真正的当选领导人。他将自己比作解放人物，如戴高乐和委内瑞拉的玛丽亚·科里娜·马查多等人。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: Interesting. OK, lots of questions here. One is this - do we know how he managed to leave Brazil and get to the U.S.?
paragraphs.zh: 萨默斯：有趣。好吧，这里有很多问题。其中一个是——我们知道他是怎么离开巴西并到达美国的吗？

paragraphs.en: KAHN: Argentine officials reported he crossed into the country last night, but Brazilian officials say they have no record of him crossing. Bolsonaro also has an Italian passport. From Argentina, he flew to Ecuador and then on to Miami. And in his letter today, he thanked Argentina's president, Javier Milei, for his support. And Milei is a far-right ally of Bolsonaro and Trump. And like Trump, Milei has still not recognized Brazil's election results. Trump was asked just a little while ago what he thought of Bolsonaro declaring himself leader of Brazil. Trump said he wasn't going to comment on that.
paragraphs.zh: KAHN：阿根廷官员报告说他昨晚进入了该国，但巴西官员表示他们没有他的入境记录。博尔索纳罗还持有意大利护照。他从阿根廷飞往厄瓜多尔，然后再飞往迈阿密。在他今天的信中，他感谢阿根廷总统哈维尔·米莱的支持。米莱是博尔索纳罗和特朗普的极右翼盟友。像特朗普一样，米莱仍未承认巴西的选举结果。就在不久前，有人问特朗普他对博尔索纳罗自称巴西领导人有何看法，特朗普表示他不会对此发表评论。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: Got it. Why did Brazil's federal police revoke his passport?
paragraphs.zh: 萨默斯：明白了。巴西联邦警察为什么要吊销他的护照？

paragraphs.en: KAHN: That order came from a Supreme Court justice who said Bolsonaro was a flight risk because he's facing several investigations, and that justice oversaw the case against Bolsonaro's father, Jair. In his letter today, Flávio said that Brazil's judiciary has been, quote, "weaponized" against his entire family. The cases against Bolsonaro include a money laundering scheme tied to online gambling. Another involves questionable financing of a biopic about his father. Bolsonaro denies any wrongdoing.
paragraphs.zh: 卡恩：这个命令来自一位最高法院大法官，他说博尔索纳罗有逃跑风险，因为他正面临多项调查，而这位大法官曾负责审理针对博尔索纳罗的父亲贾伊尔的案件。在今天的信中，弗拉维奥表示，巴西的司法系统已经，被引用的话说，是“被武器化”来对付他的整个家族。针对博尔索纳罗的案件包括涉及网络赌博的洗钱计划。另一个案件涉及他父亲传记片的可疑融资。博尔索纳罗否认有任何不当行为。

articles.dek: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase "Sí, se puede!" that became a widespread…

paragraphs.en: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase "Sí, se puede!" that became a widespread rallying cry, has died. She was 96.
paragraphs.zh: 多洛雷斯·韦尔塔，共同创立了联合农场工人工会，以改善全国水果和蔬菜田地的工作条件，并创造了“Sí, se puede!”这一成为广泛号召口号的短语，已去世，享年96岁。

paragraphs.en: Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home.
paragraphs.zh: 胡尔塔的家人在她的基金会发表的一份声明中表示，她于周三在家中去世。

paragraphs.en: She kept a busy schedule well into her 90s, marching in protests and speaking in cities across the country about race, poverty, LGBTQ+ and women's rights on behalf of her Bakersfield, California-based foundation.
paragraphs.zh: 她一直忙碌到九十多岁，参加抗议活动，并在全国各城市就种族、贫困、LGBTQ+和女性权利发言，代表她位于加利福尼亚贝克斯菲尔德的基金会。

paragraphs.en: Huerta's resolve cemented her place in history as one of the nation's most influential labor leaders, civil rights icons and feminist activists. Her three-word Spanish-language slogan — which translates to "Yes, it can be done" — was grounded in the belief that people could affect change.
paragraphs.zh: 胡埃尔塔的决心巩固了她在历史上的地位，成为国家最有影响力的劳工领袖、民权偶像和女权主义活动家之一。她的三字西班牙语口号——意为“是的，可以做到”——基于人们能够带来改变的信念。

paragraphs.en: Her work over the decades earned her a number of accolades, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor. When then-President Barack Obama presented the award in 2012, he praised Huerta as a tenacious leader and joked that he had stolen her slogan for his 2008 campaign.
paragraphs.zh: 她几十年来的工作为她赢得了许多荣誉，包括总统自由勋章——国家最高平民荣誉。当时的总统巴拉克·奥巴马在2012年颁发这一奖项时，称赞胡尔塔是一个坚韧不拔的领袖，并开玩笑说他在2008年的竞选活动中借用了她的口号。

paragraphs.en: This year, Huerta sent shockwaves through the Latino community when she revealed that she was sexually abused in the 1960s by the farmworker movement's co-founder, César Chavez, leading to the birth of two children, a secret she kept for 60 years and long after he died.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，当胡尔塔透露她在1960年代被农工运动的共同创始人塞萨尔·查韦斯性虐待并因此生下两个孩子时，她在拉美裔社区引起了震惊，这是她保密了60年的秘密，直到查韦斯去世很久之后才被揭露。

paragraphs.en: From the early 1970s on, Huerta's life partner was Richard Chavez, César's brother, and together they had four kids. She also had seven children from two earlier marriages.
paragraphs.zh: 从1970年代初起，胡埃尔塔的生活伴侣是理查德·查韦斯，塞萨尔的兄弟，他们一起有四个孩子。她在两次早期婚姻中还有七个孩子。

paragraphs.en: Huerta said she had kept silent for so long because she feared that coming forward would compromise her life's work and unravel all the progress made for workers.
paragraphs.zh: 胡埃尔塔说，她之所以长期保持沉默，是因为她担心站出来会危及她一生的工作，并破坏为工人所取得的所有进展。

articles.title: How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio
articles.dek: Candidates work to ease concerns as data centers become hot-button issue for Ohioans

paragraphs.en: Candidates work to ease concerns as data centers become hot-button issue for Ohioans
paragraphs.zh: 随着数据中心成为俄亥俄州民众关注的热点问题，候选人努力缓解人们的担忧

paragraphs.en: MT. ORAB, Ohio — The data center mystery in this rural exurb of Cincinnati has consumed Nick Owens.
paragraphs.zh: 俄亥俄州奥拉布山——位于辛辛那提这个乡村远郊的数据中心之谜让尼克·欧文陷入困扰。

paragraphs.en: The lifelong Republican and self-described small-town attorney has spent countless hours trying to figure out what's going on with 1,000 acres of farmland and trees that property records show were sold to a data center developer in 2024 and 2025.
paragraphs.zh: 这位毕生都是共和党的、自称小镇律师的人花了无数小时试图弄清楚那块农田和树林出了什么问题，房产记录显示这些土地在2024年和2025年被出售给了一家数据中心开发商，总面积达1000英亩。

paragraphs.en: In a few spots, the data center property runs right up against beautiful two-story homes.
paragraphs.zh: 在一些地方，数据中心的财产紧邻漂亮的两层住宅。

paragraphs.en: "This is the Ohio that people brag about. This is the Ohio people love. This is the small town charm," he says. "Living in the rural area, but getting the benefits of a nice, lovely neighborhood."
paragraphs.zh: “这是人们夸耀的俄亥俄州。这是人们热爱的俄亥俄州。这就是小镇的魅力，”他说。“生活在农村地区，但享受美好、宜人的社区带来的好处。”

paragraphs.en: Some of the most coordinated opposition to data centers anywhere in the country grew out of what happened in secrecy in this village of 4,300 people, a short drive up a country road from Owens' home.
paragraphs.zh: 全国一些对数据中心最有组织的反对，起源于在这个只有4300人的村庄里秘密发生的事情，这个村庄距离欧文斯的家沿乡间小路开车不远。

paragraphs.en: Nondisclosure agreements have stymied Owens' efforts to learn more. But along his quest, he crossed paths with another local attorney and a real estate agent who were equally alarmed. Together, they mobilized a network of volunteers in nearly all 88 counties in the state. They are Democrats, Republicans and Independents. They called themselves Conserve Ohio.
paragraphs.zh: 保密协议阻碍了欧文斯了解更多情况的努力。但在他的探索过程中，他遇到了另一位当地律师和一位同样感到震惊的房地产经纪人。他们一起动员了几乎全州88个县的志愿者网络。他们包括民主党人、共和党人和独立人士。他们称自己为“保护俄亥俄”。

paragraphs.en: "We all share the same ethos and the same passion for preserving our way of life, preserving the future of Ohio, frankly, from the hyperscale data center invasion," says Owens. "It's really beautiful."
paragraphs.zh: 欧文斯说：“我们都有相同的精神和相同的热情，致力于保护我们的生活方式，保护俄亥俄州的未来，坦率地说，是免受超大规模数据中心的入侵。这真的很美。”

articles.title: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
articles.dek: The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration is proposing to dramatically scale back a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry at drilling sites nationwide.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府正在提议大幅缩减拜登时代的一项规则，该规则旨在减少全国范围内钻探现场石油和天然气行业的甲烷排放。

paragraphs.en: Methane is a major contributor to climate change and is estimated to be 80 times more planet-warming than carbon dioxide in a twenty-year time frame. In 2023, the Biden administration finalized rules that were meant to rein in methane emissions from the oil and gas sector.
paragraphs.zh: 甲烷是导致气候变化的主要因素，据估计，在二十年的时间范围内，其对地球变暖的影响是二氧化碳的 80 倍。2023 年，拜登政府最终敲定了旨在限制油气部门甲烷排放的规定。

paragraphs.en: President Trump made the announcement while campaigning in Lubbock, Texas, Tuesday, saying his administration's revision, under the Clean Air Act, would save the industry billions in production costs and spur more domestic drilling. The proposal comes as Republicans face a backlash from voters over high gas prices heading into the midterms.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普总统在周二于德克萨斯州拉伯克的竞选活动中宣布，他的政府根据《清洁空气法》进行的修订将为行业节省数十亿美元的生产成本，并刺激更多的国内钻探。这一提议正值共和党人在中期选举前因高油价而面临选民的强烈反弹。

paragraphs.en: "Behind every barrel of oil and every cubic foot of natural gas produced in the U.S. are millions of workers, businesses, and the heartbeat of this nation's economy. The Biden EPA destructively targeted all this," EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said in a press release.
paragraphs.zh: 美国环保局局长李·泽尔丁在一份新闻稿中表示：“在美国生产的每一桶石油和每一立方英尺的天然气背后，都有数百万工人、企业以及这个国家经济的脉搏。拜登政府的环保局以破坏性的方式针对了这一切。”

paragraphs.en: The oil and gas industry, which vigorously opposed the 2023 rules, said EPA's proposed rollback will address some of the challenges companies have faced in trying to comply with the regulations.
paragraphs.zh: 积极反对2023年规则的石油和天然气行业表示，环保局提议的撤销将解决公司在尝试遵守这些法规时面临的部分挑战。

paragraphs.en: "We look forward to working with the Trump administration on a more workable approach that supports American energy production, provides greater regulatory certainty and advances continued emissions reductions," Dustin Meyer, vice president at the American Petroleum Institute, a trade organization for the U.S. oil and gas industry, said in a statement.
paragraphs.zh: 美国石油协会（一家美国石油和天然气行业的贸易组织）副总裁达斯汀·迈耶在一份声明中表示：“我们期待与特朗普政府合作，采取一种更可行的方法，支持美国能源生产，提供更大的监管确定性，并推进持续的减排。”

paragraphs.en: But environmentalists say this may end up actually costing the industry more.
paragraphs.zh: 但环保人士表示，这实际上可能会让行业花费更多。

paragraphs.en: "Methane is natural gas, or natural gas is methane," says Jon Goldstein, associate vice president at the Environmental Defense Fund. "And so if you're capturing more natural gas, you're not allowing it to leak out, you're not allowing it to be flared, you have more product that you can sell. And so that offsets a lot of the costs."
paragraphs.zh: 环境保护基金副总裁乔恩·戈德斯坦说：“甲烷就是天然气，或者说天然气就是甲烷。因此，如果你捕获了更多的天然气，你就不会让它泄漏，也不会让它被燃烧掉，你将有更多可以出售的产品。这就抵消了很多成本。”

articles.title: Despite her own hard times, a Maryland woman became a leading data center activist
articles.dek: Despite her hard financial times, a Maryland woman became a leading local data center activist — an example of the way the issue has prompted people to get involved.

paragraphs.en: Despite her hard financial times, a Maryland woman became a leading local data center activist — an example of the way the issue has prompted people to get involved.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管她经济困难，一位马里兰州的女性仍成为当地数据中心的主要活动家——这是这一问题促使人们参与的一个例子。

paragraphs.en: The backlash against data centers has inspired newcomers to get involved in civic activism, like one woman in Prince George's County, Maryland, who got more involved despite facing a lot of challenges in her own life. Jenny Abamu of member station WAMU in Washington, D.C., reports.
paragraphs.zh: 针对数据中心的反对引发了新手参与公民行动的热情，比如马里兰州乔治王子县的一位女性，尽管她自身生活中面临许多挑战，但仍更加积极参与其中。华盛顿特区会员电台 WAMU 的珍妮·阿巴穆报道。

paragraphs.en: JENNY ABAMU, BYLINE: The overgrown grass and weeds seem to stretch into the horizon, nearly 90 acres of empty land in Landover, Maryland, in a predominantly Black community. It had been Landover Mall, which closed in 2002. Then, in 2024, the same developer that built the mall won approval from county planners for a $5 billion data center campus. Taylor Frazier McCollum, who lived less than a mile away, described the moment she learned about the development.
paragraphs.zh: 珍妮·阿巴姆（JENNY ABAMU），署名：茂密的草和杂草似乎延伸到地平线，在马里兰州兰多弗的约90英亩空地上，这片区域主要是黑人社区。这原本是兰多弗购物中心，但在2002年关闭。然后，在2024年，建设该商场的同一开发商获得了县规划部门批准，建造一个价值50亿美元的数据中心园区。住在不到一英里外的泰勒·弗雷泽·麦考勒姆（Taylor Frazier McCollum）描述了她得知该开发项目时的那一刻。

paragraphs.en: TAYLOR FRAZIER MCCOLLUM: I was like, oh, hell, no. Why would you want to bring water-polluting, diesel-generating, like, data centers right down the street from where people live, work, play? Like, it just - it didn't make sense to me.
paragraphs.zh: 泰勒·弗雷泽·麦考勒姆：我当时想，哦，绝不。你为什么要把污染水源、产生柴油排放的数据中心建在离人们生活、工作、娱乐的地方这么近呢？这对我来说根本讲不通。

paragraphs.en: ABAMU: Frazier McCollum isn't the typical land use protester, the not in my backyard homeowner. She doesn't own a home. In fact, in 2024, as a single mother, her and her young daughter were evicted from their rental. She worked at a waxing center that reduced its wages, and she fell behind on her rent. Since then, they've moved around.
paragraphs.zh: ABAMU：弗雷泽·麦考勒姆不是典型的土地使用抗议者，也不是那种‘不要在我家后院建’的房主。她没有房子。事实上，在2024年，作为单亲母亲，她和年幼的女儿从租住的房子中被驱逐。她在一家脱毛中心工作，该中心降低了工资，她因此拖欠了房租。从那以后，她们一直在搬来搬去。

paragraphs.en: FRAZIER MCCOLLUM: It was difficult. It was just hard for me because I created this ideal life, paying for us to live in this apartment and have our own space. And then to have it taken away, it felt like something that wasn't ever going to end.
paragraphs.zh: 弗雷泽·麦考勒姆：这很困难。对我来说很难，因为我创造了这种理想的生活，支付我们的公寓住房并拥有我们自己的空间。然后当这一切被剥夺时，感觉像是永远不会结束的事情。

paragraphs.en: ABAMU: They lived in her grandfather's home when she learned about the proposed project. She created a petition, gaining over 25,000 signatures, leading to widely attended protests and culminating with moratoriums on data centers throughout the county, blocking the $5 billion project. She went to county meetings, testified at the state capitol and endorsed political candidates. Along the way, she found herself an unusual coalition, socialists, environmentalists, neighbors angry about their electricity bills. Staci Hartwell, a long-term environmental activist, said she struggled to get traction on the data centers until Frazier McCollum came along.
paragraphs.zh: ABAMU：她在得知拟议项目时住在她祖父的家里。她发起了一份请愿书，收集了超过25,000个签名，导致广泛参与的抗议活动，并最终促使整个县对数据中心实施了暂停，阻止了50亿美元的项目。她参加了县议会会议，在州议会作证，并支持政治候选人。在此过程中，她找到了一个不同寻常的联盟，包括社会主义者、环保主义者以及对电费感到愤怒的邻居。长期环保活动家Staci Hartwell表示，在Frazier McCollum出现之前，她在数据中心问题上一直难以取得进展。

paragraphs.en: STACI HARTWELL: This is something that was happening in her neighborhood. And it was really like her awakening.
paragraphs.zh: 斯塔西·哈特韦尔：这是发生在她社区的事情。这确实像是她的觉醒。
