articles.title: U.S. to issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro as his whereabouts remain unclear
articles.dek: RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil — The United States says it will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family, amid multiple reports that the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate has left the…

paragraphs.en: RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil — The United States says it will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family, amid multiple reports that the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate has left the country following Sunday's election. His whereabouts have not been independently confirmed.
paragraphs.zh: 巴西里约热内卢--美国表示将向弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗（ Flávio Bolsonaro ）及其家人发放签证，多起报道称，这位被击败的巴西总统候选人在周日大选后离开了该国。他的下落尚未得到独立证实。

paragraphs.en: Bolsonaro, a conservative politician and ally of President Donald Trump, lost Sunday's presidential election to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by more than four million votes, just three weeks after winning the first round. While Bolsonaro's Liberal Party has since recognized Lula's victory, Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat.
paragraphs.zh: 保守派政治家、唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统的盟友博尔索纳罗(Bolsonaro)在周日的总统选举中输给了现任总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦(Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva) ，在赢得第一轮投票仅三周后虽然博尔索纳罗的自由党此后承认了卢拉的胜利，但博尔索纳罗拒绝承认失败。

paragraphs.en: On Tuesday a senior U.S. administration official said that the State Department would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family, allowing them to enter the country.
paragraphs.zh: 周二，美国政府一名高级官员表示，国务院将向博尔索纳罗及其家人发放签证，允许他们入境。

paragraphs.en: The visa announcement comes as Bolsonaro faces multiple investigations in Brazil, including allegations of money laundering and tax evasion, which he denies. On Monday Brazil's Supreme Court ordered him to surrender his passports within 24 hours and barred him from leaving the country.
paragraphs.zh: 签证公告发布之际， Bolsonaro在巴西面临多项调查，包括洗钱和逃税指控，他对此予以否认。周一，巴西最高法院命令他在24小时内交出护照，并禁止他离开该国。

paragraphs.en: The order followed comments by Bolsonaro's brother Eduardo, who lives in self-imposed exile in Florida, suggesting Flávio should leave Brazil if he lost the election.
paragraphs.zh: 该命令是在博尔索纳罗的兄弟爱德华多发表评论之后发布的，他住在佛罗里达州的自我流放中，他建议弗拉维奥如果他输掉选举，应该离开巴西。

paragraphs.en: In a video released that day, Bolsonaro said federal police officers had stopped him outside the home of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, and ordered him to surrender his passports. The former far-right leader is under house arrest after being sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup following his own defeat by Lula in the 2022 presidential election.
paragraphs.zh: 在当天发布的一段视频中，博尔索纳罗说，联邦警察在他父亲、前总统贾尔·博尔索纳罗（ Jair Bolsonaro ）的家外拦住了他，并命令他交出护照。这位前极右翼领导人因在2022年总统大选中被卢拉击败后策划政变而被判处27年监禁后被软禁。

paragraphs.en: "I never thought about leaving the country," Flávio Bolsonaro said in the video. "I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this aberration." He described the order as an attempt to intimidate him.
paragraphs.zh: “我从未想过要离开这个国家，”弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗在视频中说。“我将交出我的护照，保护自己免受这种失常的影响。“他将这一命令描述为企图恐吓他。

paragraphs.en: On Tuesday, Brazilian media reported that Bolsonaro had left for the United States. His campaign manager, his lawyer and other political allies had earlier said they did not know his whereabouts.
paragraphs.zh: 周二，巴西媒体报道称，博尔索纳罗已前往美国。他的竞选经理、律师和其他政治盟友早些时候曾表示，他们不知道他的下落。

articles.title: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices
articles.dek: In the summer of 2020, I lived briefly in Ithaca, New York. It's the only time I've lived near Aldi, the grocery store known for low prices. I went twice, and I thought it was fine, but…

paragraphs.en: In the summer of 2020, I lived briefly in Ithaca, New York. It's the only time I've lived near Aldi, the grocery store known for low prices. I went twice, and I thought it was fine, but underwhelming. I appreciated the low prices, but it didn't have everything I needed. The store was small and a bit shabby.
paragraphs.zh: 2020年夏天，我短暂地住在纽约伊萨卡。这是我唯一一次住在以低价闻名的杂货店Aldi附近。我去过两次，我觉得没关系，但很平淡。我很欣赏低廉的价格，但它没有我所需要的一切。商店很小，有点破旧。

paragraphs.en: I didn't know it yet, but those are the exact ingredients that have made Aldi the fastest-growing grocery chain in America. Per Bloomberg, Aldi plans to have more than 3,000 American locations by the end of 2028, which would be more than any other chain but Walmart. In 2024, Aldi generated some $29 billion in U.S. sales, which is more than Trader Joe's.
paragraphs.zh: 我还不知道，但这些正是使Aldi成为美国增长最快的杂货连锁店的原因。据彭博社报道， Aldi计划到2028年底在美国拥有3,000多家门店，这将超过沃尔玛以外的任何其他连锁店。2024年， Aldi在美国的销售额约为290 $ ，超过了Trader Joe's。

paragraphs.en: Aldi is a German company known for having low, low prices, and it deserves that reputation. Food reporter Deena Shanker told me for my podcast Gastronomics that her experience comparison shopping over many months was that Aldi either matched Walmart on price or was a bit cheaper. Grocers like Wegmans and Kroger have announced defensive price reductions, and an analysis published in late 2023 of Lidl, another German grocer with a very similar model to Aldi's but fewer U.S. stores, found that grocery chains reduced their markups ~7 percent in areas where Lidl stores opened.
paragraphs.zh: Aldi是一家以低价、低价而闻名的德国公司，它理应享有这样的声誉。美食记者Deena Shanker为我的播客Gastronomics告诉我，她几个月的购物体验比较表明， Aldi要么在价格上与沃尔玛相匹配，要么更便宜。像Wegmans和Kroger这样的杂货商已经宣布了防御性降价，另一家与Aldi的模式非常相似但美国商店较少的德国杂货商Lidl在2023年底发布的一项分析发现，在Lidl商店开业的地区，杂货连锁店的加价降低了约7%。

paragraphs.en: All to say: Aldi is disrupting the grocery business and actually lowering prices even as the cost of food—at restaurants and other grocery stores—goes up and up.
paragraphs.zh: 总而言之： Aldi正在扰乱生鲜杂货业务，实际上正在降低价格，即使餐厅和其他生鲜杂货店的食品成本不断上涨。

paragraphs.en: Maybe this sounds a bit humdrum. But I found it totally intriguing and perplexing, because…
paragraphs.zh: 也许这听起来有点单调乏味。但我发现它非常有趣和令人困惑，因为……

paragraphs.en: - Walmart and Costco's business models depend on low prices, too, and they can offer low prices by having huge stores, giant warehouses, and incredible economies of scale that allow them to pay less for Oreo's, baby carrots, and Jif peanut butter than other grocers. So how the heck is Aldi matching or beating them on price?
paragraphs.zh: -沃尔玛和Costco的商业模式也依赖于低价，他们可以通过拥有大型商店、巨型仓库和令人难以置信的规模经济来提供低价，这使他们能够比其他杂货店支付更少的奥利奥、小胡萝卜和Jif花生酱的费用。那么， Aldi在价格上是如何匹配或击败他们的呢？

paragraphs.en: - When a company disrupts a longstanding industry, it's typically a startup enabled by new technology—like Netflix using online streaming to disrupt Blockbuster and video rental. But Aldi is not staffed by futuristic robots. Its stores just look like grocery stores, and Aldi was founded 80 years ago, in post-war Germany. So what's going on?
paragraphs.zh: -当一家公司颠覆一个长期存在的行业时，它通常是由新技术支持的创业公司，例如Netflix使用在线流媒体来颠覆Blockbuster和视频租赁。但Aldi没有未来主义机器人。它的商店看起来就像杂货店， Aldi于80年前在战后德国成立。到底是怎么回事？

paragraphs.en: - One of the proudest achievements of America's capitalistic market economy is providing its citizens an abundance of increasingly affordable food. Somewhat famously, Soviet leader Boris Yeltsin toured a grocery store in Houston during the Cold War and was amazed that the average American enjoyed more variety than top Soviet politicians. From 1960 to 2019, Americans spent less and less of their income on food each year, even as they enjoyed more frequent restaurant meals, more sushi, and far better beer. But since the pandemic, food has become less affordable. Can American markets no longer provide cheap groceries? Did something break?
paragraphs.zh: -美国资本主义市场经济最自豪的成就之一是为其公民提供越来越实惠的食物。众所周知，苏联领导人鲍里斯·叶利钦（ Boris Yeltsin ）在冷战期间参观了休斯顿的一家杂货店，并惊讶地发现，普通美国人比苏联顶级政治家更喜欢多样化。从1960年到2019年，美国人每年花在食品上的收入越来越少，尽管他们在餐厅用餐更频繁，寿司更多，啤酒更好。但自疫情爆发以来，食物变得越来越便宜。美国市场能否不再提供廉价的生鲜杂货？有什么东西坏了吗？

paragraphs.en: One necessary but not sufficient explanation for Aldi's low prices is that management is obsessed with efficiency and cutting unnecessary costs. There's no music in stores, because speakers (and licensing fees for muzak) cost money. The staff places products on shelves still in the cardboard boxes they were trucked in on, because artfully unpacking fruits, bread, and jerky sticks would mean higher labor costs. The shabbiness is intentional — it's the cost of cheaper groceries.
paragraphs.zh: Aldi低价的一个必要但不充分的解释是，管理层痴迷于效率和削减不必要的成本。商店里没有音乐，因为扬声器（以及muzak的许可费）需要花钱。工作人员仍将产品放在货架上的纸箱中，因为巧妙地拆开水果、面包和肉干棒意味着更高的劳动力成本。破旧是故意的—这是更便宜的生鲜杂货的成本。

articles.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
articles.dek: Polymarket has investigated "dozens" of bets on its prediction markets related to the midterm election, according to the company's head of global intelligence and investigations, Shana Bautista.

paragraphs.en: Polymarket has investigated "dozens" of bets on its prediction markets related to the midterm election, according to the company's head of global intelligence and investigations, Shana Bautista.
paragraphs.zh: Polymarket的全球情报和调查主管Shana Bautista表示，该公司已经调查了与中期选举相关的“数十个”预测市场押注。

paragraphs.en: At least two of these Polymarket investigations have been referred to its regulator, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, according to a person who is familiar with the probes, but not authorized to speak publicly about them.
paragraphs.zh: 据一位熟悉调查的人士称，这些Polymarket调查中至少有两项已提交给其监管机构美国商品期货交易委员会，但无权公开谈论这些调查。

paragraphs.en: These investigations into election insider trading and manipulation come as prediction market Polymarket — and its chief competitor Kalshi — have exploded in popularity over the past year. But the fast-growing industry also faces significant legal challenges from states and political pushback from lawmakers who argue betting on the outcome of elections poses serious risks to the democratic process.
paragraphs.zh: 这些对选举内幕交易和操纵的调查是在预测市场Polymarket及其主要竞争对手Kalshi在过去一年中爆发的情况下进行的。但快速增长的行业也面临着来自各州的重大法律挑战，以及来自立法者的政治阻力，他们认为押注选举结果对民主进程构成严重风险。

paragraphs.en: In April, Kalshi banned and fined a handful of political candidates from betting on themselves. A month later, NPR reported that campaign staffers had made "thousands" using insider polling information to bet on their own candidates on platforms like Polymarket and PredictIt.
paragraphs.zh: 今年4月， Kalshi禁止并罚款了一些政治候选人对自己下注。一个月后， NPR报道称，竞选工作人员利用内幕民意调查信息在Polymarket和PredictIt等平台上对自己的候选人下注。

paragraphs.en: Polymarket's Bautista — a former FBI official and cryptocurrency analyst — told NPR her team of 16 and a new election surveillance system are actively policing election bets ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms.
paragraphs.zh: Polymarket的包蒂斯塔（ Bautista ）是前联邦调查局官员和加密货币分析师，她告诉NPR ，她的16人团队和一个新的选举监控系统正在积极监督11月3日中期选举之前的选举投注。

paragraphs.en: "If you have information that you have a duty to protect, don't trade on it," Bautista said. "It's explicitly against our terms of use on both platforms, but also is against the law. If you decide that you are smarter and can do it, we will find you."
paragraphs.zh: 包蒂斯塔说： “如果你有责任保护的信息，不要利用这些信息进行交易。” “这明显违反了我们在这两个平台上的使用条款，但也违反了法律。如果你认为自己更聪明，可以做到，我们会找到你。”

paragraphs.en: Bautista joined Polymarket in June. She oversees information gathered from both the U.S.-regulated version of Polymarket, which requires users to provide their real identities, and its bigger brother, Polymarket International, which is essentially unregulated and where trading can be done anonymously and with cryptocurrency. Despite this, Bautista said crypto trades are rarely completely anonymous.
paragraphs.zh: Bautista于6月加入Polymarket。她负责监督从美国监管版本的Polymarket （要求用户提供真实身份）和其较大的兄弟Polymarket International （基本上不受监管，可以匿名使用加密货币进行交易）收集的信息。尽管如此， Bautista表示，加密货币交易很少是完全匿名的。

paragraphs.en: "There's never been a case that we work where we haven't been able to identify, potentially, who these people are," Bautista said.
paragraphs.zh: Bautista说： “从来没有一个案例是我们无法确定这些人是谁。”

articles.dek: PRESTON, Md. — It's lunchtime at Preston Elementary School, on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Kids file in, get dollops of food on their segmented trays, and maybe grab a chocolate milk. But one option…

paragraphs.en: PRESTON, Md. — It's lunchtime at Preston Elementary School, on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Kids file in, get dollops of food on their segmented trays, and maybe grab a chocolate milk. But one option on today's menu is special, served alongside grapes and broccoli.
paragraphs.zh: 马里兰州普雷斯顿—现在是马里兰州东海岸普雷斯顿小学的午餐时间。孩子们挤进来，在他们的分段托盘上放一些食物，也许还会拿一杯巧克力牛奶。但今天菜单上的一种选择是特别的，与葡萄和西兰花一起供应。

paragraphs.en: "I got a catfish sandwich!" announces Ben Rochon, a second-grader. Between mouthfuls, he tells me how it is: "It's yummy."
paragraphs.zh: 二年级学生Ben Rochon说： “我有一个鲶鱼三明治！”在两口之间，他告诉我是怎么回事： “真好吃。”

paragraphs.en: He's eating a catfish cake, also known by its nickname, the "catty patty." Some kids like it with ketchup or mayo. Fifth-grader Teagan Donovan goes minimal.
paragraphs.zh: 他正在吃一个鲶鱼蛋糕，也被称为“鲶鱼馅饼”。“有些孩子喜欢吃番茄酱或蛋黄酱。五年级学生Teagan Donovan的成绩很低。

paragraphs.en: "I like it by itself with no toppings, because it's pretty good by itself," she says. In Teagan's case, "by itself" is literal: "I ignore the bun."
paragraphs.zh: “我喜欢它本身没有配料，因为它本身就很好，”她说。在Teagan的案例中， “本身”是字面上的： “我忽略了面包。”

paragraphs.en: Not everyone's into the fish cake — after all, this sunny Friday is also pizza day at Preston, and cheese slices are tough competition. But more kids have been trying catfish when it's served a couple of times a month. That's good news to Beth Brewster, who oversees food services for Caroline County Public Schools.
paragraphs.zh: 不是每个人都喜欢吃鱼饼--毕竟，这个阳光明媚的星期五也是普雷斯顿的披萨日，奶酪片是激烈的竞争。但越来越多的孩子每月都会尝试几次鲶鱼。这对负责卡罗琳县公立学校餐饮服务的Beth Brewster来说是个好消息。

paragraphs.en: "It tastes great. It's great for you," she says of the fish cake.
paragraphs.zh: “味道很棒，对你来说很棒，”她谈到鱼饼时说。

paragraphs.en: It has another benefit: It's made with blue catfish. Since spreading to the Chesapeake Bay in recent decades, the fish has become an apex predator. It can grow to more than 100 pounds; its voracious appetite is fueling worries that it's eating too many native species.
paragraphs.zh: 它还有另一个好处：它是用蓝鲶鱼制成的。自从最近几十年蔓延到切萨皮克湾以来，这种鱼已经成为顶级捕食者。它可以长到100磅以上；它贪婪的食欲加剧了人们对它吃太多本土物种的担忧。

paragraphs.en: "It tastes so good because it eats everything we love — crabs and rockfish, and all kinds of things that we love to eat," Brewster says.
paragraphs.zh: “它味道好极了，因为它吃我们爱吃的一切——螃蟹、石斑鱼，以及我们爱吃的各种东西，”布鲁斯特说。

articles.title: Romantasy fans turn out for 'Midnight Maas' release event
articles.dek: The latest book in Sarah J. Maas' A Court of Thorns and Roses (known as ACOTAR by its fans) series came out on Tues., October 27. The night before its release, thousands of fans flooded big box…

paragraphs.en: The latest book in Sarah J. Maas' A Court of Thorns and Roses (known as ACOTAR by its fans) series came out on Tues., October 27. The night before its release, thousands of fans flooded big box and indie bookshops alike for midnight release parties across the country.
paragraphs.zh: 莎拉· J ·马斯（ Sarah J. Maas ）的《荆棘与玫瑰的宫廷》（ A Court of Thorns and Roses ，粉丝们称之为ACOTAR ）系列的最新， 10月27日。发行前一天晚上，成千上万的粉丝涌入大盒子和独立书店，参加全国各地的午夜发行派对。

paragraphs.en: At Politics and Prose in Washington, D.C., dozens of fans perused the bookshelves in tight leather costumes, pointy faerie ears and sparkly tiaras, waiting to get their hands on A Court of Splintered Harmony.
paragraphs.zh: 在华盛顿特区的Politics and Prose ，数十名粉丝穿着紧身皮革服装、尖尖的仙女耳朵和闪闪发光的头饰仔细阅读书架，等待着获得A Court of Splintered Harmony。

paragraphs.en: Dalia Luque is one of the eager readers who attended the event. A Monday night might not sound like the opportune time for a party running from 10 p.m. to midnight — after all, she could have preordered the book online — but Luque said she wanted to experience this moment with other fans.
paragraphs.zh: Dalia Luque是参加此次活动的热心读者之一。对于从晚上10点到午夜的派对来说，周一晚上听起来可能不是合适的时间--毕竟，她本可以在网上预订这本书--但卢克说，她想和其他粉丝一起体验这一时刻。

paragraphs.en: "I just want to have fun with the community and get to share with my friends as we read along," Luque said.
paragraphs.zh: 卢克说：“我只是想和社区一起玩得开心，并且在我们一起阅读的过程中与朋友们分享。”

paragraphs.en: Fans waiting to get their hands on the new book passed the time playing trivia, making friendship bracelets, getting their faces painted and enjoying champagne.

articles.title: A quick guide to Israel's high-stakes elections
articles.dek: TEL AVIV, Israel — Israel is holding pivotal elections on Tuesday in what many Israelis call the most consequential vote in their country's history after the last few years of war.

paragraphs.en: TEL AVIV, Israel — Israel is holding pivotal elections on Tuesday in what many Israelis call the most consequential vote in their country's history after the last few years of war.
paragraphs.zh: 以色列特拉维夫——以色列将在周二举行关键选举，许多以色列人称这是该国历史上最重要的投票，此前几年经历了战争。

paragraphs.en: Polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu trailing in the race behind his main challenger, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. But it may take weeks or months before it's clear who will be designated the winner.
paragraphs.zh: 民意调查显示，总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡在竞选中落后于他的主要竞争对手、前军方首长加迪·埃泽科特。但可能需要数周或数月时间才能明确谁将被指定为胜利者。

paragraphs.en: That's because voters will not directly choose between Netanyahu and Eisenkot. Instead, they will vote for one of a dozen main parties running for office in the 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset.
paragraphs.zh: 那是因为选民不会直接在内塔尼亚胡和艾森科特之间做出选择。相反，他们会投票给参加120个议席议会（称为克内塞特）选举的十几个主要政党之一。

paragraphs.en: The real contest will begin after election day, when party leaders try to assemble a governing coalition of at least 61 lawmakers.
paragraphs.zh: 真正的较量将在选举日之后开始，那时各党派领导人将尝试组建至少有61名议员的执政联盟。

paragraphs.en: Here is a guide to the leading candidates, the issues shaping the vote and what could happen next.
paragraphs.zh: 这里是关于主要候选人、影响投票的议题以及接下来可能发生的情况的指南。

paragraphs.en: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, is seeking another term in office.
paragraphs.zh: 以色列历任最久的总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡正在寻求连任。

paragraphs.en: Netanyahu has led the most right-wing government in Israel's history. His coalition has included Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, leaders of far-right, religious nationalist parties that are also running in this election, as well as two ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties.
paragraphs.zh: 内塔尼亚胡领导了以色列历史上最右翼的政府。他的联盟包括伊塔马尔·本-格维尔和贝扎列尔·斯莫特里奇，这两位极右翼宗教民族主义党派的领导人也在参加此次选举，以及两个极端正统犹太党派。

paragraphs.en: Netanyahu has led Israel through more than three years of war and regional conflict, from the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023, and the war in Gaza to fighting involving Lebanon, Iran, Syria and Yemen. He is campaigning on Israel's military achievements and his close relationship with President Trump, who recently endorsed him. Netanyahu has also made confronting Iran, and ultimately seeking the fall of its regime, a central part of his campaign.
paragraphs.zh: 内塔尼亚胡领导以色列度过了三年多的战争和地区冲突，从2023年10月7日哈马斯发动的袭击和加沙战争，到涉及黎巴嫩、伊朗、叙利亚和也门的战斗。他的竞选以色列的军事成就以及他与特朗普总统的密切关系为基础，特朗普最近还对他表示支持。内塔尼亚胡还将对抗伊朗、最终寻求其政权倒台作为竞选的核心部分。

paragraphs.en: His principal challenger is Gadi Eisenkot, a former chief of staff of the Israeli military who is running for prime minister for the first time as the leader of a new center-right party called Yashar, Hebrew for "Straight" or "Upright."
paragraphs.zh: 他的主要挑战者是加迪·艾森科特，以色列军方前参谋长，他首次以新成立的中右翼政党“雅沙尔”（希伯来语意为“正直”或“直立”）的领导人身份竞选总理。

articles.title: AI giant Anthropic files for an IPO that could break records
articles.dek: The artificial intelligence startup Anthropic, maker of the hugely popular Claude AI models, has taken a major step toward holding an initial public offering that analysts expect to be one of the…

paragraphs.en: The artificial intelligence startup Anthropic, maker of the hugely popular Claude AI models, has taken a major step toward holding an initial public offering that analysts expect to be one of the biggest ever.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能初创公司Anthropic，Claude AI模型的制造商，本已迈出了走向首次公开募股的重要一步，分析师预计这将成为有史以来最大的一次公开募股之一。

paragraphs.en: Anthropic filed final paperwork with regulators on Monday for an IPO under the ticker symbol ANT that reports have said could value the company at between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion.
paragraphs.zh: Anthropic周一向监管机构提交了首次公开募股（IPO）的最终文件，股票代码为ANT，据报道，这次IPO可能使公司的估值在1.5万亿到2万亿美元之间。

paragraphs.en: That would put it in league with Elon Musk's rocketry and AI company SpaceX, which was valued at around $1.8 trillion when it listed in June. Anthropic's listing prospectus did not say how many shares the company will offer or at what price range.
paragraphs.zh: 这将使其与埃隆·马斯克的火箭和人工智能公司SpaceX齐名，SpaceX在6月上市时的估值约为1.8万亿美元。Anthropic的上市招股说明书没有说明公司将提供多少股份或价格区间。

paragraphs.en: The filing of a public version of a registration statement called a Form S-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission is a major milestone in Anthropic's meteoric rise. It was launched just five years ago by a breakaway group of OpenAI researchers, led by Dario Amodei, who were concerned that that company, run by Sam Altman, was not on a path to develop AI safely.
paragraphs.zh: 向证券交易委员会提交一份名为S-1表格的注册声明的公开版本，是Anthropic快速崛起的一个重要里程碑。该公司仅在五年前由一群脱离OpenAI的研究人员创立，领导者是Dario Amodei，他们担心由Sam Altman管理的公司并未走在安全开发人工智能的道路上。

paragraphs.en: Anthropic has since become a juggernaut, and OpenAI's biggest competitor, with some of the most widely used AI models on the market. But the company has faced controversy, including a conflict with the Pentagon over how its models can be used and questions about Amodei's dire warnings on AI risks.
paragraphs.zh: 自那以后，Anthropic 已经成为一个巨头，也是 OpenAI 最大的竞争对手，拥有一些市场上最广泛使用的 AI 模型。但该公司也面临争议，包括与五角大楼就其模型的使用方式发生冲突，以及关于 Amodei 对 AI 风险的严重警告提出的问题。

paragraphs.en: Still, the prospectus highlighted Anthropic's bullishness about the technology. "We believe this abundance of AI will rapidly transform every sector of the global economy in ways greater than the impact of industrialization, electricity, semiconductors, and the internet," it said.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管如此，招股说明书仍强调了Anthropic对该技术的乐观态度。招股说明书中写道：“我们相信，这种人工智能的丰富性将迅速以比工业化、电力、半导体和互联网更大的方式改变全球经济的各个领域。”

paragraphs.en: In its prospectus, Anthropic highlighted breakneck growth — in revenue, income and losses. The company said its revenue in the first half of the year rose 1,300% at $16.3 billion, while its adjusted operating income — a measure of potential profitability — hit $1.6 billion during the period, vs. a loss of $1.8 billion the year before.
paragraphs.zh: 在其招股说明书中，Anthropic 强调了其收入、收益和亏损的极速增长。公司表示，今年上半年其收入增长了 1300%，达到 163 亿美元，而其调整后的营业收入——一种潜在盈利能力的衡量标准——在此期间达到了 16 亿美元，而去年同期则为 18 亿美元的亏损。

paragraphs.en: Anthropic has yet to turn an annual profit, and said it booked a loss of nearly $81 billion in the January to June period, up from $13 billion during the same six months last year.
paragraphs.zh: Anthropic 目前尚未实现年度盈利，并表示在一月至六月期间录得近 810 亿美元的亏损，相较于去年同期的 130 亿美元有所上升。

articles.title: Fired OpenAI researchers say independent safety audits aren't going well
articles.dek: In their first interview since being fired, OpenAI safety researchers Mikita Balesni and Tomek Korbak say they were terminated for prioritizing safety over the short-term interests of the company.

paragraphs.en: In their first interview since being fired, OpenAI safety researchers Mikita Balesni and Tomek Korbak say they were terminated for prioritizing safety over the short-term interests of the company.
paragraphs.zh: 在被解雇后的第一次采访中，OpenAI 的安全研究员米基塔·巴莱斯尼和托梅克·科尔巴克表示，他们是因为将安全置于公司短期利益之上而被解雇的。

paragraphs.en: We're going to hear now from two former safety researchers at OpenAI. They were let go earlier this month because OpenAI says an internal investigation found they mishandled sensitive information.
paragraphs.zh: 现在我们将听取两位前 OpenAI 安全研究人员的意见。由于 OpenAI 表示内部调查发现他们处理敏感信息不当，他们本月早些时候被解雇。

paragraphs.en: But the researchers say they were following standard practices in communicating with outside groups, including an independent nonprofit organization called METR that audits the work of AI companies. That group was investigating what went wrong this summer when autonomous OpenAI agents went rogue and launched a coordinated cyberattack against another AI platform, Hugging Face.
paragraphs.zh: 但研究人员表示，他们在与外部机构沟通时遵循了标准做法，包括一个名为 METR 的独立非营利组织，该组织审计 AI 公司的工作。该组织正在调查今年夏天自动化 OpenAI 代理失控并对另一个 AI 平台 Hugging Face 发动协调网络攻击时出错的原因。

paragraphs.en: Now the researchers, Mikita Balesni and Tomek Korbak, have spoken to tech journalists Kevin Roose and Casey Newton. They are the hosts of Machine Gods, a new podcast from NPR. Let's listen to a little bit of their conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，研究人员Mikita Balesni和Tomek Korbak已经与科技记者Kevin Roose和Casey Newton进行了交谈。他们是NPR新播客《Machine Gods》的主持人。让我们听一听他们的一小段对话。

paragraphs.en: CASEY NEWTON: So let's talk about one of the key events that it seems like, you know, may have led to you guys being fired, which is this Hugging Face incident. I'd love to hear a little bit about what it was like to be working at OpenAI when that happened. Do you remember where you were when you learned what was going on, and what was the reaction?
paragraphs.zh: CASEY NEWTON：那么让我们来谈谈其中一个关键事件，这个事件似乎可能导致你们被解雇，那就是 Hugging Face 事件。我很想了解一下那个时候在 OpenAI 工作是什么感觉。你还记得你当时在哪里得知发生了什么吗？大家的反应是怎样的？

paragraphs.en: TOMEK KORBAK: Yeah, it was a very intense time. I remember telling Mikita that everything that I was preparing for earlier in my career was finally real. Everything before was a drill. And now that thing is actually happening, and it actually matters a lot.
paragraphs.zh: 托梅克·科尔巴克：是的，那是一段非常紧张的时期。我记得我告诉米基塔，我早期职业生涯中所准备的一切终于成真了。以前的一切都是演习。而现在这件事真的发生了，而且真的非常重要。

paragraphs.en: ROOSE: Right. And around that time, OpenAI decides to invite in these researchers from METR and Redwood Research to study this event. How were you both working with these outside researchers who were invited in to do this investigation?
paragraphs.zh: ROOSE：没错。就在那个时候，OpenAI 决定邀请 METR 和 Redwood Research 的这些研究人员来研究这次事件。你们俩是如何与这些被邀请来进行调查的外部研究人员合作的？

paragraphs.en: KORBAK: So initially METR was supposed to be on premises just for two days. And then when they started looking at the data, our understanding of the scale of incident was still evolving, so we've actually been learning that there is actually more, so we invited them for a second visit. When they realized that there is actually even more, and we invited them for a third visit.
paragraphs.zh: KORBAK：所以最初METR本来只打算在现场待两天。然后，当他们开始查看数据时，我们对事件规模的理解仍在不断发展，所以我们实际上了解到情况比想象的更多，因此我们邀请他们进行了第二次访问。当他们意识到情况实际上更严重时，我们又邀请他们进行了第三次访问。

articles.title: A Kelvin wave raised sea levels on the West Coast. More are coming
articles.dek: One of the first major signs of this year's "Super El Niño" has reached the U.S. It's called a Kelvin wave – a deep ocean wave that's currently raising sea levels along the West Coast.

paragraphs.en: One of the first major signs of this year's "Super El Niño" has reached the U.S. It's called a Kelvin wave – a deep ocean wave that's currently raising sea levels along the West Coast.
paragraphs.zh: 今年“超级厄尔尼诺”的第一个主要迹象已经到达美国。这被称为开尔文波——一种深海波，目前正在抬高西海岸的海平面。

paragraphs.en: Scientists have long known about Kelvin waves, but this year, the phenomena grabbed the public's attention with video explanations receiving thousands of views across TikTok and X.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家们早就知道开尔文波，但今年，这一现象通过视频讲解吸引了公众的注意，在抖音和X上获得了数千次观看。

paragraphs.en: "It does surprise me – I mean, here it's been around all this time," says Mark Cane, who created one of the first models to forecast and predict El Niño. "I'm sure Lord Kelvin is happy in his grave."
paragraphs.zh: “这确实让我感到惊讶——我是说，这里一直存在了这么久，”曾创建最早的厄尔尼诺预测模型之一的马克·凯恩说。“我敢肯定开尔文勋爵在坟墓里也会感到高兴。”

paragraphs.en: (Lord Kelvin, the British physicist who also developed the Kelvin temperature scale, first described the wave back in the late 1800s.)
paragraphs.zh: (英国物理学家开尔文勋爵，同时也是开尔文温度计量表的发明者，最早在19世纪末描述了这种波动。)

paragraphs.en: Kelvin waves can develop along the equator during El Niño years, when a vast region of water in the Pacific Ocean becomes much warmer than usual.
paragraphs.zh: 在厄尔尼诺年份，当太平洋的一个广阔水域比平常温暖得多时，开尔文波可以沿赤道发展。

paragraphs.en: Some of this warm water, in the form of a Kelvin wave that stretches thousands of miles, moves slowly east beneath the ocean's surface until it reaches South America. Then it splits, traveling north along the West Coast and as far south as Chile.
paragraphs.zh: 其中一些暖水以跨越数千英里的开尔文波形式，缓慢地沿着海洋表面下向东移动，直到到达南美洲。然后它分开，一部分沿西海岸向北移动，另一部分向南移动，直至智利。

paragraphs.en: "It's like an enormous bathtub sloshing around," Cane says, professor emeritus of earth and climate sciences at Columbia University. "But the slosh is very peculiar, because it only goes west to east along the equator in a Kelvin wave."
paragraphs.zh: “这就像一个巨大的浴缸在晃动，”哥伦比亚大学地球与气候科学名誉教授凯恩说。“但这种晃动非常特殊，因为它只沿赤道从西向东移动，是一种开尔文波。”

paragraphs.en: These are not the massive, highly visible waves that crash into shorelines during major storms and hurricanes.
paragraphs.zh: 这些并不是在重大风暴和飓风期间冲击海岸线的巨大、非常明显的浪潮。

articles.title: These 'Seven Stories About Tammy' add up to one brilliant piece of writing
articles.dek: I've been thinking a lot lately about the famous opening sequence of Up, the Pixar animated film. That movie begins with a wordless montage of a marriage, Carl and Ellie's marriage: its youthful…

paragraphs.en: I've been thinking a lot lately about the famous opening sequence of Up, the Pixar animated film. That movie begins with a wordless montage of a marriage, Carl and Ellie's marriage: its youthful giddiness, the pain of infertility and the long goodbye of Ellie's death in old age.
paragraphs.zh: 最近我一直在思考皮克斯动画电影《飞屋环游记》中著名的开场序列。那部电影以一段无言的蒙太奇开始，讲述了卡尔和埃莉的婚姻：年轻时的喜悦、不孕的痛苦，以及埃莉老去去世时的长久告别。

paragraphs.en: The montage takes less than four-and-a-half minutes and, yet, contains the emotional depths of a much longer film or novel about a marriage. Relying solely on words, Elizabeth McCracken's Seven Stories About Tammy does much the same for the family saga.
paragraphs.zh: 这个蒙太奇不到四分半钟，但却包含了关于婚姻的更长电影或小说所具有的情感深度。仅仅依靠文字，伊丽莎白·麦克雷肯的《七个关于泰米的故事》也为家族传奇做了同样的事情。

paragraphs.en: As its title bluntly announces, Seven Stories About Tammy is composed of seven interrelated short stories about a family's encounters with their eldest son's girlfriend and eventual wife, an older woman named Tammy. McCracken's story sequence has appeared earlier in a literary magazine, as well as in the 2025 anthology of The Best American Short Stories. But, having it available in standalone book form is just the right vessel for this family montage. Not every piece of fiction, after all, fits into the prefab format of a novel or a single short story. The only downside is that this 70-page book is so tiny — the size of a pamphlet, really — that I misplaced it repeatedly around my house. Whenever I found it again, though, I felt like something rich and strange had been returned to me out of the jumble of the mundane.
paragraphs.zh: 正如其标题直言不讳地宣告的那样，《七个关于塔米的故事》由七个相互关联的短篇小说组成，讲述了一个家庭与长子女友、最终成为他妻子的年长女子塔米的遭遇。麦克拉肯的故事系列此前已在文学杂志上发表，并收录在2025年的《美国最佳短篇小说选集中》。不过，将其作为单行本出版，是呈现这个家庭群像的最佳形式。毕竟，并非每一篇小说都适合套用小说或单篇短篇小说的现成格式。唯一的缺点是，这本70页的小书实在太小——实际上只有小册子的大小——以至于我在家里经常把它放错地方。但每次再次找到它时，我都感觉像一些丰富而奇异的东西从日常的杂乱中归还给了我。

paragraphs.en: We first meet Tammy when the Harkin family does: in the mid-1970s when eldest son, Morris, who's been living in Florida, brings her home to Boston for dinner. Here's our omniscient narrator describing that first encounter:
paragraphs.zh: 我们第一次见到塔米，是和哈金家族一起：在1970年代中期，当长子莫里斯——一直住在佛罗里达——带她回波士顿吃晚饭时。以下是我们无所不知的叙述者对那次初次相遇的描述：

paragraphs.en: They had never met anyone from Florida, only people who ended up there, as if by gravity. Tammy was tall and angular, stood with her hands in her own back pockets — blue jeans, ironed. Morris’s jeans were ironed now, too. By her? Or had she put Morris to work at the ironing board? She seemed like that sort of woman, efficient and ruthless, with beautiful manners.
paragraphs.zh: 他们从未遇到过佛罗里达的人，只遇到那些最后落到那里的人的，好像被引力吸引一样。塔米高挑且骨感，双手插在自己后面的口袋里——蓝色牛仔裤，熨得平整。莫里斯的牛仔裤现在也熨平了。是她弄的吗？还是她让莫里斯去熨裤子了？她看起来就是那种女人，高效而无情，举止优雅。

paragraphs.en: On that evening, the family "parlor game" of "how old is she?" will begin, because, we're flatly told: "Morris was twenty-seven. She wasn't."
paragraphs.zh: 在那个晚上，家里的“客厅游戏”——“她几岁了？”——将会开始，因为我们被明确告知：“莫里斯二十七岁。她不是。”

paragraphs.en: In the third story, set about 15 years later, insecure middle child, Victoria, visits Tammy and Morris, now married, at their high-rise apartment in Philadelphia. Victoria, who's struggled with see-sawing weight all her young life, is served a shallow bowl of soup. Here's some dinner table dialogue:
paragraphs.zh: 在第三个故事中，时间大约设定在15年后，不自信的中间孩子维多利亚拜访了塔米和莫里斯，他们现在已经结婚，住在费城的高层公寓里。维多利亚一生中一直为体重的上下波动而烦恼，她被端来一个浅浅的汤碗。以下是餐桌上的一些对话：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no thank you!” [Victoria] said. “I’m saving room for dinner.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，不，谢谢！”[维多利亚]说。“我得留肚子吃晚饭。”
